one_line_idea: Similarity graphs leak the images: releasing only a kNN graph or similarity matrix of a private image collection allows attribute and identity recovery through graph-structure matching against public references.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] The local geometry of a similarity graph is a fingerprint of its underlying content: aligning a released private graph to a graph built over public references (graph matching on degree, neighborhood, and motif statistics) recovers which public-like items private nodes correspond to, leaking categories, rare attributes, and sometimes identities, with leakage growing with graph degree.

full_record.one_line_idea: Similarity graphs leak the images: releasing only a kNN graph or similarity matrix of a private image collection allows attribute and identity recovery through graph-structure matching against public references.
full_record.problem: [KNOWN FACT] Research and industry share derived artifacts of private image sets (similarity graphs, cluster assignments, retrieval indices) as if discarding vectors and pixels makes the release safe.
full_record.core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] The local geometry of a similarity graph is a fingerprint of its underlying content: aligning a released private graph to a graph built over public references (graph matching on degree, neighborhood, and motif statistics) recovers which public-like items private nodes correspond to, leaking categories, rare attributes, and sometimes identities, with leakage growing with graph degree.
full_record.falsifiable_prediction: [EXPECTED RESULT] Graph-matching attacks on kNN graphs (k between 10 and 50) of a private subset embedded in a population overlapping public references will correctly categorize at least 40% of nodes and identify at least 10% of exact public duplicates from structure alone, with both rates rising in k; the idea is falsified if node categorization stays under 15% (near coarse priors) at k of 50, showing graph structure is effectively anonymous.
full_record.why_important: It closes a loophole in data-release thinking: derived-artifact sharing is currently exempt from image-privacy review, and a demonstrated structure-leak with a degree-response makes the risk quantifiable and policy-relevant.
full_record.why_possibly_novel: [MODEL SPECULATION / unverified] Graph de-anonymization is developed for social networks; its transfer to image-similarity graphs with embedding-mediated reference matching appears unexplored.
full_record.minimal_falsification_experiment: Build kNN graphs over private splits of public datasets, give the attacker only graph structure plus a disjoint public reference pool, implement structural matching, and score category and duplicate recovery versus k.
full_record.main_risk: Success may hinge on the private set overlapping public content; for truly out-of-distribution private collections, structure matching could collapse to chance.
full_record.community_default_belief: [MODEL SPECULATION] Similarity graphs and indices are treated as anonymized derivatives, safe to share once vectors and images are withheld.
full_record.why_it_might_be_wrong: Local graph geometry may be too generic across image collections (most neighborhoods look alike) for reliable matching at realistic scales.
full_record.fastest_falsification_experiment: Graph construction and matching over public datasets, one A100 mostly for embedding: about 1-2 GPU-days.

one_line_idea: A contamination inflation law: benchmark-score inflation is a fittable function of duplication count, similarity level, and model scale, turning contamination audits from binary accusations into quantitative score corrections.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Score inflation from contamination follows a smooth dose-response in (duplication count, similarity to test item, model scale) that can be fitted once with controlled injections and then applied to audit findings to produce corrected scores with stated uncertainty, because the underlying mechanism (per-item memorization strength) is itself dose-dependent.

full_record.one_line_idea: A contamination inflation law: benchmark-score inflation is a fittable function of duplication count, similarity level, and model scale, turning contamination audits from binary accusations into quantitative score corrections.
full_record.problem: [KNOWN FACT] Benchmark contamination in web-scale pretraining is discussed as a binary defect (contaminated or not), and audits report overlap counts without a validated way to translate overlap into points of score inflation.
full_record.core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Score inflation from contamination follows a smooth dose-response in (duplication count, similarity to test item, model scale) that can be fitted once with controlled injections and then applied to audit findings to produce corrected scores with stated uncertainty, because the underlying mechanism (per-item memorization strength) is itself dose-dependent.
full_record.falsifiable_prediction: [EXPECTED RESULT] An inflation law fitted on controlled injections in one model family will predict measured inflation in a second family within 30% relative for at least 8 of 10 dose conditions; the idea is falsified if cross-family predictions err by over 70% relative on half the conditions, showing inflation is too idiosyncratic to model.
full_record.why_important: Every contamination audit today ends with an unquantified shadow over reported results; a transferable inflation law converts audits into corrected leaderboards and settles how-much-does-it-matter disputes with numbers.
full_record.why_possibly_novel: [MODEL SPECULATION / unverified] Contamination effects have been measured in isolated language-model studies; a fitted, cross-family-validated inflation law for vision benchmarks appears absent.
full_record.minimal_falsification_experiment: Inject eval-similar images (exact, near-duplicate, same-scene strata) at controlled counts into pretraining corpora for two small model families, measure per-stratum score inflation on the corresponding benchmarks, fit the law on family A, and validate on family B.
full_record.main_risk: Inflation may interact with fine-tuning and prompting details downstream of pretraining, adding variance that the three-variable law cannot capture.
full_record.community_default_belief: [MODEL SPECULATION] Contamination is treated as disqualifying but unquantifiable, so results are either defended as probably fine or dismissed wholesale.
full_record.why_it_might_be_wrong: Inflation may be dominated by benchmark-specific item structure (some items are far more memorable), defeating any low-dimensional law.
full_record.fastest_falsification_experiment: 4-6 small pretrains with stratified injections plus evaluation, one A100: about 6 GPU-days on public data.

one_line_idea: Contamination grows a generalization halo with scale: at small scale contaminated items inflate only their own scores, but at larger scale the benefit spreads to related uncontaminated items, blurring the line between cheating and learning.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Small models memorize contaminated items as isolated lookups, but larger models integrate them into representations that transfer to neighboring test items (same category, similar scenes), so the contamination benefit acquires a halo whose radius grows with scale, and decontaminated-subset scores are themselves inflated at large scale.

full_record.one_line_idea: Contamination grows a generalization halo with scale: at small scale contaminated items inflate only their own scores, but at larger scale the benefit spreads to related uncontaminated items, blurring the line between cheating and learning.
full_record.problem: [KNOWN FACT] Contamination audits assume the damage is localized to leaked items, and decontaminated-subset evaluation is the accepted fix; whether contamination benefits spread beyond the leaked items is untested.
full_record.core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Small models memorize contaminated items as isolated lookups, but larger models integrate them into representations that transfer to neighboring test items (same category, similar scenes), so the contamination benefit acquires a halo whose radius grows with scale, and decontaminated-subset scores are themselves inflated at large scale.
full_record.falsifiable_prediction: [EXPECTED RESULT] Injection experiments across a scale ladder will show benefit on non-injected neighbor items rising from under 0.3 points at the smallest rung to over 1 point at the largest, with benefit decaying in similarity distance; the idea is falsified if neighbor benefit stays under 0.3 points at all scales (contamination stays localized and decontaminated evaluation is sound).
full_record.why_important: If halos exist, the standard remove-the-leaked-items remedy under-corrects at exactly the scales that matter, and contamination accounting must switch from item lists to similarity neighborhoods.
full_record.why_possibly_novel: [MODEL SPECULATION / unverified] Localized contamination effects are assumed in audit methodology; the scale-dependent halo hypothesis with similarity-decay measurement appears untested.
full_record.minimal_falsification_experiment: Inject a subset of benchmark-similar items at fixed dose across a 3-rung ladder, and measure score changes on injected items, similarity-ranked neighbors, and dissimilar controls per rung.
full_record.main_risk: Neighbor benefit must be separated from generic data-addition benefit via content-matched non-benchmark injection controls.
full_record.community_default_belief: [MODEL SPECULATION] Contamination effects are assumed confined to leaked items, making subset decontamination a complete fix.
full_record.why_it_might_be_wrong: Representation integration may require far more exposures than realistic contamination provides, keeping halos negligible at all practical scales.
full_record.fastest_falsification_experiment: 3 small pretrains with injections and control arms, one A100: about 5-6 GPU-days; all data drawn from public corpora.

one_line_idea: U-shaped scaling exists in vision and its trough is movable by data: tasks where a shortcut is learned before the true feature show worse-then-better scale curves, and enriching disambiguating data shifts the trough to smaller scale.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] When a task admits a shortcut that mid-scale models can exploit but that fails on the evaluation (texture instead of shape, context instead of object, canonical-pose assumptions), scale curves dip while the shortcut dominates and recover once capacity plus data suffice to learn the true feature, and the trough location is set by the ratio of shortcut-supporting to shortcut-breaking examples, so data enrichment moves it.

one_line_idea: Aggregate scaling laws over-promise for rare slices: per-slice exponents are strongly heterogeneous, aggregate fits are dominated by head slices, and tail-slice performance is systematically over-predicted by the global law.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Per-slice scaling exponents vary by multiples across frequency-defined strata, with tail slices showing flatter exponents than the aggregate fit implies (their improvement depends on rare-data growth, not total-data growth), so global-law extrapolations systematically overstate tail progress by a predictable margin.

full_record.one_line_idea: Aggregate scaling laws over-promise for rare slices: per-slice exponents are strongly heterogeneous, aggregate fits are dominated by head slices, and tail-slice performance is systematically over-predicted by the global law.
full_record.problem: [KNOWN FACT] Scaling laws are fitted on aggregate benchmark scores, and their extrapolations are quoted as if all input strata improve together, while deployment risk concentrates precisely in rare slices.
full_record.core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Per-slice scaling exponents vary by multiples across frequency-defined strata, with tail slices showing flatter exponents than the aggregate fit implies (their improvement depends on rare-data growth, not total-data growth), so global-law extrapolations systematically overstate tail progress by a predictable margin.
full_record.falsifiable_prediction: [EXPECTED RESULT] Fitting per-slice curves on frequency-stratified evaluations across a data-scaling grid will find bottom-decile-slice exponents at most half the aggregate exponent, and aggregate-law extrapolation will over-predict measured tail-slice accuracy at 8x data by at least 3 points; the idea is falsified if per-slice exponents cluster within 30% of the aggregate and tail over-prediction is under 1 point.
full_record.why_important: Safety cases and product plans quote aggregate scaling as evidence that rare-case failures will scale away; slice-wise accounting either validates or numerically corrects that inference.
full_record.why_possibly_novel: [MODEL SPECULATION / unverified] Slice-based evaluation is standard in fairness and robustness work; connecting it to scaling-law extrapolation error as a fitted decomposition appears missing.
full_record.minimal_falsification_experiment: Pretrain across 4 data sizes, evaluate on frequency-stratified slices of standard benchmarks, fit aggregate and per-slice laws, and compare extrapolation errors at the largest size.
full_record.main_risk: Slice definitions based on estimated frequency carry measurement error that could exaggerate exponent heterogeneity; bootstrap over slice assignments is required.
full_record.community_default_belief: [MODEL SPECULATION] Aggregate scaling curves are consumed as if uniform across the input distribution, with tail improvement assumed to track the headline exponent.
full_record.why_it_might_be_wrong: Representation sharing may genuinely propagate head-slice gains to tail slices, homogenizing exponents more than the frequency logic predicts.
full_record.fastest_falsification_experiment: 4 small pretrains plus stratified evaluation, one A100: about 4 GPU-days; all data drawn from public corpora.

one_line_idea: Scaling breaks are data-determined, not architecture-determined: the data scale at which scaling curves bend is shared across architecture families trained on the same corpus, identifying breaks as corpus properties.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Curve breaks reflect exhaustion of specific information strata in the corpus (novelty depletion, tail exhaustion, resolution floors), so break locations in data-scale coincide across ConvNet and ViT families trained identically on the same corpus, and shift together when the corpus is re-composed.

full_record.one_line_idea: Scaling breaks are data-determined, not architecture-determined: the data scale at which scaling curves bend is shared across architecture families trained on the same corpus, identifying breaks as corpus properties.
full_record.problem: [KNOWN FACT] Scaling-curve irregularities (bends, plateaus) are routinely attributed to architectural limitations, motivating architecture churn, without testing whether the break locations belong to the data rather than the model.
full_record.core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Curve breaks reflect exhaustion of specific information strata in the corpus (novelty depletion, tail exhaustion, resolution floors), so break locations in data-scale coincide across ConvNet and ViT families trained identically on the same corpus, and shift together when the corpus is re-composed.
full_record.falsifiable_prediction: [EXPECTED RESULT] Break locations fitted per architecture family on the same nested corpora will agree within 1.5x in data scale across families, while a re-composed corpus (tail-enriched) will move both families' breaks by at least 2x in the same direction; the idea is falsified if break locations differ by over 4x across architectures on identical data, showing breaks are architectural.
full_record.why_important: If breaks are corpus properties, the correct response to a plateau is data re-composition rather than architecture replacement, redirecting a chronic pattern of misplaced engineering effort.
full_record.why_possibly_novel: [MODEL SPECULATION / unverified] Scaling comparisons across architectures exist for smooth regions; alignment testing of break locations as a data-attribution method appears novel territory.
full_record.minimal_falsification_experiment: Pretrain small ConvNet and ViT ladders on identical nested corpora and one re-composed variant, fit piecewise scaling curves, and compare break locations across the four conditions.
full_record.main_risk: Break detection is statistically fragile; pre-registered piecewise-fitting criteria and bootstrap confidence intervals on break locations are essential.
full_record.community_default_belief: [MODEL SPECULATION] Plateaus and bends in scaling curves are read as evidence that the architecture has run out of capacity or expressiveness.
full_record.why_it_might_be_wrong: Architectures may hit genuinely different information bottlenecks (attention versus convolutional receptive-field limits), giving family-specific breaks even on identical data.
full_record.fastest_falsification_experiment: About 16 small pretrains (2 families x 4 sizes x 2 corpora) plus curve fitting, one A100: about 7 GPU-days; at the high end but feasible; all data drawn from public corpora.

one_line_idea: More data can hurt minorities of the distribution: at fixed mixture, growing total data amplifies majority-domain dominance and can reduce absolute accuracy on minority domains, a non-monotonicity fixable by share re-weighting, not by more data.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] With fixed mixture weights, scaling total data grows the majority-domain gradient signal proportionally while minority-domain representations face increasing competitive pressure for shared capacity, so beyond a threshold, minority-domain accuracy declines in absolute terms even as aggregate accuracy improves, and share re-weighting at the same total data eliminates the decline.

full_record.one_line_idea: More data can hurt minorities of the distribution: at fixed mixture, growing total data amplifies majority-domain dominance and can reduce absolute accuracy on minority domains, a non-monotonicity fixable by share re-weighting, not by more data.
full_record.problem: [KNOWN FACT] Data growth under a fixed collection mixture is universally assumed at-worst-neutral for every subpopulation, and minority-domain regressions between model releases are treated as accidents rather than a predictable scaling phenomenon.
full_record.core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] With fixed mixture weights, scaling total data grows the majority-domain gradient signal proportionally while minority-domain representations face increasing competitive pressure for shared capacity, so beyond a threshold, minority-domain accuracy declines in absolute terms even as aggregate accuracy improves, and share re-weighting at the same total data eliminates the decline.
full_record.falsifiable_prediction: [EXPECTED RESULT] In fixed-mixture scaling runs spanning 16x total data with a 2% minority domain, minority-domain accuracy will peak and then decline by at least 2 points by the largest scale while aggregate accuracy rises, and a re-weighted arm at the largest scale will recover the minority peak within 1 point; the idea is falsified if minority accuracy is monotone non-decreasing in total data (within 0.5 points) at fixed mixture.
full_record.why_important: It would overturn the universal more-data-is-safe assumption at the subpopulation level, explain cross-release regressions that currently look like bugs, and hand corpus owners a costless fix (re-weighting) with measured effect.
full_record.why_possibly_novel: [MODEL SPECULATION / unverified] Capacity competition and majority dominance are known qualitatively in multi-task settings; the absolute-decline-with-total-data prediction at fixed mixture for vision pretraining appears untested.
full_record.minimal_falsification_experiment: Pretrain across nested total-data sizes at fixed mixture including a tagged 2% minority domain, evaluate minority-domain probes per size, and run a re-weighted control at the largest size.
full_record.main_risk: The effect size likely depends on model capacity relative to data; a capacity-matched second ladder is needed to show the decline is not an artifact of one undersized model.
full_record.community_default_belief: [MODEL SPECULATION] Scaling data at fixed composition is believed to help every subpopulation, or at worst leave minorities flat.
full_record.why_it_might_be_wrong: Shared-feature transfer from majority growth may keep lifting minority domains indefinitely, making the predicted decline unobservable at feasible scales.
full_record.fastest_falsification_experiment: 5-6 small pretrains over nested sizes plus a re-weighted arm, one A100: about 5 GPU-days on public data.

one_line_idea: A paired same-image comparison protocol for detectors, using per-image score differences with sign-flip permutation tests, shrinks comparison uncertainty enough to change published accept/reject conclusions at fixed test-set size.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Because per-image difficulty is the dominant variance component and is shared between models evaluated on the same images, a paired design that tests the distribution of per-image metric differences removes that shared component and yields far tighter confidence intervals than image-level bootstrap of each model separately.

full_record.one_line_idea: A paired same-image comparison protocol for detectors, using per-image score differences with sign-flip permutation tests, shrinks comparison uncertainty enough to change published accept/reject conclusions at fixed test-set size.
full_record.problem: [KNOWN FACT] Detector comparisons report unpaired AP deltas on a shared test set, and small claimed gains (under 0.5 AP) are routinely accepted without any variance accounting.
full_record.core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Because per-image difficulty is the dominant variance component and is shared between models evaluated on the same images, a paired design that tests the distribution of per-image metric differences removes that shared component and yields far tighter confidence intervals than image-level bootstrap of each model separately.
full_record.falsifiable_prediction: [EXPECTED RESULT] On COCO val2017, paired sign-flip confidence intervals for AP-proxy differences between five nearby public detector pairs will be at least 2x narrower than unpaired bootstrap intervals, and at least one of the five pairs will flip between significant and not-significant relative to the unpaired protocol; kill the idea if the average interval-width ratio is under 1.3x or if zero of five pairs change status.
full_record.why_important: This is a direct debunk-to-repair conversion: instead of another audit showing detection deltas are noise, it ships a drop-in comparison protocol that makes small-margin conclusions defensible without collecting new data.
full_record.why_possibly_novel: [MODEL SPECULATION / unverified] Paired tests are standard in ML broadly, but a pre-registered paired-permutation protocol for COCO-style AP with a measured interval-shrinkage factor and conclusion-flip audit appears unpublished for detection.
full_record.minimal_falsification_experiment: Evaluate 10 public detectors on COCO val2017, compute per-image matched-detection quality scores, then compare paired sign-flip intervals against unpaired bootstrap intervals for all 45 pairs and count status flips among the 5 closest pairs.
full_record.main_risk: AP is a set-level statistic that does not decompose exactly into per-image contributions, so the paired proxy may rank models slightly differently than corpus-level AP and the repair could be rejected on faithfulness grounds.
full_record.community_default_belief: [MODEL SPECULATION] Practitioners treat the shared test set as already controlling for difficulty and assume reported AP deltas are comparable without explicit pairing.
full_record.why_it_might_be_wrong: If between-image variance is small relative to within-image matching noise, pairing buys little and interval widths will barely change.
full_record.fastest_falsification_experiment: Inference of 10 MMDetection model-zoo checkpoints (e.g., Faster R-CNN, RetinaNet, DETR, YOLOX variants) on COCO val2017 plus permutation statistics runs in under 8 hours on one consumer GPU; all data and models public.

one_line_idea: A reference-decoder evaluation contract that pins score thresholds, NMS behavior, and max-detections into a single frozen decoding specification makes detector rankings invariant across evaluation harnesses.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Cross-harness rank instability is caused almost entirely by the unpinned decoding stage (thresholding, NMS, caps), not by metric arithmetic, so shipping a frozen reference decoder that consumes raw logits/boxes will eliminate harness-induced rank flips.

full_record.problem: [KNOWN FACT] The same detector checkpoint can receive different AP values and even different rankings under different evaluation harnesses because score thresholds, NMS variants, and per-image detection caps differ across implementations.
full_record.core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Cross-harness rank instability is caused almost entirely by the unpinned decoding stage (thresholding, NMS, caps), not by metric arithmetic, so shipping a frozen reference decoder that consumes raw logits/boxes will eliminate harness-induced rank flips.
full_record.falsifiable_prediction: [EXPECTED RESULT] Across three public evaluation stacks applied to 10 public detectors on COCO val2017, at least two pairwise rank flips will occur under default decoding, and re-evaluating from raw outputs through the frozen reference decoder will reduce flips to zero; kill the idea if flips persist after pinning or if default stacks already agree on all pairs.
full_record.why_important: Converts the well-documented harness-variance complaint into an adoptable artifact: a decoding contract that makes leaderboard numbers portable across codebases.
full_record.why_possibly_novel: [MODEL SPECULATION / unverified] Harness discrepancies have been reported anecdotally, but a decoding-contract artifact with a measured before/after rank-flip count appears missing.
full_record.minimal_falsification_experiment: Export raw pre-NMS outputs for 10 detectors, evaluate with pycocotools defaults, a second public harness, and a third with altered max-dets/threshold defaults, then re-evaluate all through one pinned decoder and count pairwise rank flips before and after.
full_record.main_risk: Some architectures (end-to-end set predictors) have no natural pre-NMS raw output aligned with anchor-based models, making one shared decoding contract partially ill-defined.
full_record.community_default_belief: [MODEL SPECULATION] Researchers assume pycocotools is a de facto standard and that harness choice is a rounding-error concern.
full_record.why_it_might_be_wrong: If most modern models are evaluated through nearly identical default pipelines already, measured flips may be zero and the repair unnecessary.
full_record.fastest_falsification_experiment: Re-scoring exported detections on COCO val2017 for 10 MMDetection/Detectron2 zoo models (e.g., YOLOX, Deformable DETR, Faster R-CNN) under three harness configurations is CPU-dominated and finishes in under one day on a single workstation with one GPU for inference; all public.

one_line_idea: Error-decomposition-matched interventions: choosing the training fix whose target matches the dominant TIDE-style error type of a detector yields reliably larger gains than a mismatched fix, making error decomposition an actionable prescription rather than a diagnostic.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Error types are causally separable enough that an intervention targeting the dominant error component (e.g., an IoU-aware localization head when localization error dominates, or a stronger classification loss when classification error dominates) transfers its benefit primarily through that component, so decomposition-matched prescriptions beat mismatched ones under identical budgets.

full_record.one_line_idea: Error-decomposition-matched interventions: choosing the training fix whose target matches the dominant TIDE-style error type of a detector yields reliably larger gains than a mismatched fix, making error decomposition an actionable prescription rather than a diagnostic.
full_record.problem: [KNOWN FACT] Error decompositions in the TIDE style attribute detector AP loss to classification, localization, duplicate, background, and missed-detection components, but papers use them descriptively and pick training interventions by fashion.
full_record.core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Error types are causally separable enough that an intervention targeting the dominant error component (e.g., an IoU-aware localization head when localization error dominates, or a stronger classification loss when classification error dominates) transfers its benefit primarily through that component, so decomposition-matched prescriptions beat mismatched ones under identical budgets.
full_record.falsifiable_prediction: [EXPECTED RESULT] For two public detectors with different dominant error types on COCO, applying the matched intervention will yield at least +1.0 AP and at least twice the gain of the mismatched intervention applied to the same model; kill the idea if matched and mismatched interventions differ by less than 0.3 AP on both models.
full_record.why_important: Turns a widely cited audit instrument into a decision procedure, giving practitioners a falsifiable rule for spending a fixed training budget.
full_record.why_possibly_novel: [MODEL SPECULATION / unverified] TIDE is established as a diagnostic; a pre-registered matched-vs-mismatched prescription test appears untested.
full_record.minimal_falsification_experiment: Take a localization-error-dominant and a classification-error-dominant public detector, retrain each with both a localization-targeted and a classification-targeted intervention under identical schedules, and compare AP gains in a 2x2 design.
full_record.main_risk: Interventions interact (a better localization head can also fix duplicates), blurring the attribution and producing a mixed 2x2 outcome.
full_record.community_default_belief: [MODEL SPECULATION] Error decomposition is viewed as post-hoc storytelling with no demonstrated prescriptive power.
full_record.why_it_might_be_wrong: Dominant error types may reflect dataset properties rather than model deficiencies, so any single-model intervention moves all components together.
full_record.fastest_falsification_experiment: Four short retrainings (1x schedule) of Faster R-CNN and YOLOX on COCO train2017 with MMDetection run in about 4 single-GPU days total on an A100; TIDE-style decomposition code and all data/models are public.

one_line_idea: A minimum-detectable-difference (MDD) certificate for detection benchmarks, computed from hierarchical resampling over images and seeds, lets leaderboards refuse deltas below the resolvable threshold and changes which published improvements count as real.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Detection AP variance is dominated by a few quantifiable components (test-image sampling, training seed, nondeterministic kernels), so a benchmark can publish a single MDD number from hierarchical resampling that separates resolvable from unresolvable deltas, and applying it retroactively will reclassify a substantial fraction of small claimed gains.

full_record.one_line_idea: A minimum-detectable-difference (MDD) certificate for detection benchmarks, computed from hierarchical resampling over images and seeds, lets leaderboards refuse deltas below the resolvable threshold and changes which published improvements count as real.
full_record.problem: [KNOWN FACT] COCO-style leaderboards accept arbitrarily small AP improvements, while the run-to-run and split-to-split variability of AP is rarely quantified or disclosed.
full_record.core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Detection AP variance is dominated by a few quantifiable components (test-image sampling, training seed, nondeterministic kernels), so a benchmark can publish a single MDD number from hierarchical resampling that separates resolvable from unresolvable deltas, and applying it retroactively will reclassify a substantial fraction of small claimed gains.
full_record.falsifiable_prediction: [EXPECTED RESULT] The hierarchical MDD for COCO val2017 box AP with 3-seed training of a mid-size detector will be at least 0.25 AP, and applying the certificate to 10 sampled published deltas under 0.5 AP will flip the accept decision for at least 3 of them; kill the idea if the estimated MDD is below 0.1 AP or if the certificate flips none of the sampled deltas.
full_record.why_important: Replaces recurring noise-in-benchmarks debunks with an operational acceptance rule that any leaderboard can adopt without new annotation.
full_record.why_possibly_novel: [MODEL SPECULATION / unverified] Seed-variance complaints exist for detection, but a packaged MDD certificate with hierarchical decomposition over image sampling and seeds, plus a retroactive reclassification audit, appears missing.
full_record.minimal_falsification_experiment: Train one public detector 3 times, evaluate all seeds on 200 bootstrap replicates of val2017, fit a variance-components model, derive the MDD, then apply it to a pre-registered sample of small published COCO deltas reproduced from public checkpoints.
full_record.main_risk: MDD depends on the detector family used to estimate it, so a single certificate may under- or over-state resolvability for architectures with different variance profiles.
full_record.community_default_belief: [MODEL SPECULATION] Reviewers believe a shared test set makes any positive delta meaningful, and variance disclosure is treated as optional.
full_record.why_it_might_be_wrong: Modern long training schedules may average away seed variance, making the true MDD small and the certificate toothless.
full_record.fastest_falsification_experiment: Three 1x-schedule Faster R-CNN trainings on COCO train2017 (MMDetection) plus bootstrap scoring take about 3 single-A100 days; checkpoints for the delta audit come from the public MMDetection and Detectron2 zoos.

full_record.why_important: Benchmark compression is an enabling capability for hyperparameter sweeps, continual model audits, and green evaluation, and IRT gives it a principled statistical backbone.
full_record.why_possibly_novel: [MODEL SPECULATION / unverified] IRT-based efficient benchmarking has appeared for language-model leaderboards; a detection-specific instantiation with held-out-family generalization tests appears missing.

full_record.main_risk: Item parameters may be family-specific: images that discriminate anchor-based models may not discriminate DETR-style models, hurting generalization to unseen families.
full_record.community_default_belief: [MODEL SPECULATION] Practitioners assume trustworthy detection rankings require the full 5k val set and that subsets are only for quick sanity checks.
full_record.why_it_might_be_wrong: Detection scores per image are noisy multi-instance aggregates, which may violate IRT's unidimensional latent-ability assumption badly enough to break subset transfer.

one_line_idea: Automatic consensus completion of missing test-set annotations by heterogeneous-detector agreement reproduces most conclusion changes obtained by expensive human relabeling, turning test-set repair into a zero-annotation capability.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Most consequential ground-truth errors are omissions and coarse masks that a consensus of architecturally diverse public detectors localizes with high precision, so an agreement-gated automatic completion of the ground truth recovers the bulk of the score and ranking corrections that human relabeling produces, at negligible cost.

full_record.one_line_idea: Automatic consensus completion of missing test-set annotations by heterogeneous-detector agreement reproduces most conclusion changes obtained by expensive human relabeling, turning test-set repair into a zero-annotation capability.
full_record.problem: [KNOWN FACT] Human relabeling efforts of COCO-style ground truth (e.g., the public COCO-ReM re-annotation) changed model scores and some conclusions, but relabeling costs thousands of annotator hours per dataset.
full_record.core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Most consequential ground-truth errors are omissions and coarse masks that a consensus of architecturally diverse public detectors localizes with high precision, so an agreement-gated automatic completion of the ground truth recovers the bulk of the score and ranking corrections that human relabeling produces, at negligible cost.
full_record.falsifiable_prediction: [EXPECTED RESULT] Scoring 10 public models against consensus-completed COCO val annotations will reproduce at least 70% of the per-model score shifts (sign and at least half the magnitude) observed when scoring against the human-relabeled public reference, and at least 80% of pairwise ranking changes; kill the idea if under 40% of shifts or under 50% of ranking changes are reproduced.
full_record.why_important: If automatic completion tracks human relabeling, every benchmark gains a cheap self-repair capability and relabeling budgets can be reserved for genuinely ambiguous cases.
full_record.why_possibly_novel: [MODEL SPECULATION / unverified] Model-consensus label cleaning exists for classification; validating detection-set completion directly against a public human re-annotation as ground truth for the repair appears new.
full_record.minimal_falsification_experiment: Build consensus pseudo-annotations from 7 diverse public detectors with high-agreement gating on COCO val2017, score a disjoint set of 10 models against original, consensus-completed, and human-relabeled annotations, and compare shift/ranking reproduction rates.

one_line_idea: A seed-versus-data compute-allocation rule for trustworthy detector comparisons: given a fixed GPU budget, splitting compute across 3 short-seed replicates beats one long run for deciding between two training recipes.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] For typical recipe deltas (under 1 AP), decision accuracy is variance-limited rather than bias-limited, so replicating shorter schedules and testing the seed-averaged difference yields a higher probability of correctly ranking two recipes than a single full-schedule comparison at the same total compute.

full_record.core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] For typical recipe deltas (under 1 AP), decision accuracy is variance-limited rather than bias-limited, so replicating shorter schedules and testing the seed-averaged difference yields a higher probability of correctly ranking two recipes than a single full-schedule comparison at the same total compute.
full_record.falsifiable_prediction: [EXPECTED RESULT] In a ground-truthed testbed where the true recipe ordering is established by 9-seed full-schedule runs, the 3x(1/3-schedule) protocol will pick the correct recipe in at least 80% of resampled decision trials versus at most 65% for the 1x(full) protocol at equal compute; kill the idea if the replicate protocol's decision accuracy is not at least 8 points higher, or if short schedules invert the true ordering systematically (bias regime).
full_record.why_important: Provides an immediately usable budgeting rule that repairs the single-seed comparison pathology without demanding extra compute, aimed at everyday model development rather than leaderboards.
full_record.why_possibly_novel: [MODEL SPECULATION / unverified] Seed-variance studies exist for classification and RL; a compute-matched decision-accuracy analysis for detection recipe selection with a pre-registered allocation rule appears missing.
full_record.minimal_falsification_experiment: Choose two recipes differing by a small real effect (e.g., augmentation change on RetinaNet/COCO), run 9 full-schedule seeds each to establish ground truth, then simulate both allocation protocols by subsampling runs and count correct decisions.
full_record.main_risk: Short-schedule and full-schedule recipe orderings can genuinely differ (schedule-dependent effects), in which case replicate protocols answer the wrong question no matter their variance advantage.
full_record.community_default_belief: [MODEL SPECULATION] One careful long run per configuration is considered the gold standard for recipe decisions in detection.
full_record.why_it_might_be_wrong: If seed variance for modern long schedules is tiny (well under 0.1 AP), single runs already decide correctly and replication wastes compute.

full_record.core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Mask conventions are a low-dimensional, learnable output-space transformation rather than noise, so conditioning the decoder on an explicit convention token lets one model represent multiple conventions simultaneously without averaging them into blur, and the token direction supports interpolation between conventions.

full_record.why_important: Turns the heavily debunked convention-mismatch pathology into a deployable capability: one checkpoint that serves datasets and downstream users with different masking standards.
full_record.why_possibly_novel: [MODEL SPECULATION / unverified] Dataset-token multi-dataset training exists for combining label spaces; explicitly targeting mask-boundary conventions with an interpolation test appears new.

full_record.main_risk: The overlap set of doubly annotated images may be too small to train specialists to convergence, weakening the specialist reference point.
full_record.community_default_belief: [MODEL SPECULATION] Cross-dataset mask differences are treated as annotation noise to be averaged over, not as a controllable output dimension.
full_record.why_it_might_be_wrong: Convention differences may be category-specific and inconsistent, defeating a single global token and requiring per-class conventions that no longer fit a compact conditioning scheme.

one_line_idea: Two-pass precision-tiered annotation: labeling most of a dataset coarsely and a small fraction precisely, with a tolerance-weighted loss that knows which pixels are trustworthy, reaches near-full-precision performance at roughly half the annotation cost.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Model quality is limited by boundary-region supervision quality, not by interior pixel counts, so an explicit two-tier protocol (coarse pass everywhere, precise pass on a budgeted subset) combined with a per-pixel tolerance-weighted loss recovers nearly all of full-precision performance because the loss stops fitting the unreliable boundary band of coarse masks.

full_record.main_risk: Simulated coarseness may not match real annotator behavior (which errs structurally, not morphologically), overstating the protocol's real-world recovery rate.

one_line_idea: Pre-registered tradeoff-cone acceptance: replacing single-scalar improvement tests with a Pareto-dominance test over a declared metric cone (region overlap plus boundary quality) reverses accepted wins that traded one competence for another.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] A benchmark can pre-register an acceptance cone (the set of metric-change directions counted as improvement, e.g., non-negative in both mIoU and boundary-F with at least one strict gain), and applying cone acceptance to recent method pairs will reverse a measurable fraction of scalar-accepted wins because scalar gains frequently ride on boundary regressions.

full_record.one_line_idea: Pre-registered tradeoff-cone acceptance: replacing single-scalar improvement tests with a Pareto-dominance test over a declared metric cone (region overlap plus boundary quality) reverses accepted wins that traded one competence for another.
full_record.problem: [KNOWN FACT] Methods are accepted on scalar headline metrics (mIoU, mask-AP) even when they degrade complementary qualities like boundary sharpness, and multi-metric tables are eyeballed without a decision rule.
full_record.core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] A benchmark can pre-register an acceptance cone (the set of metric-change directions counted as improvement, e.g., non-negative in both mIoU and boundary-F with at least one strict gain), and applying cone acceptance to recent method pairs will reverse a measurable fraction of scalar-accepted wins because scalar gains frequently ride on boundary regressions.
full_record.falsifiable_prediction: [EXPECTED RESULT] Evaluating 10 public segmentation model pairs on ADE20K with mIoU and boundary-F, at least 2 scalar-accepted wins will fail cone acceptance due to a boundary-F regression exceeding 1.0 points; kill the idea if fewer than 1 in 10 wins fails the cone, meaning scalar and cone acceptance coincide in practice.
full_record.why_important: Multi-metric honesty becomes an enforceable rule rather than a table aesthetic, directly repairing the metric-gaming pathology documented by eval audits.
full_record.why_possibly_novel: [MODEL SPECULATION / unverified] Pareto reporting exists in efficiency literatures; pre-registered cone acceptance as a benchmark decision rule for segmentation quality dimensions appears new.
full_record.minimal_falsification_experiment: Score public checkpoint pairs (successive versions of popular methods) on mIoU and boundary-F, apply scalar and cone rules with bootstrap uncertainty on both metrics, and count acceptance reversals.
full_record.main_risk: Cone geometry is a governance choice; adversarial submitters could lobby for cones matching their method's profile, moving the gaming one level up.
full_record.community_default_belief: [MODEL SPECULATION] A higher headline metric is treated as an improvement by definition, with boundary quality relegated to qualitative figures.
full_record.why_it_might_be_wrong: Boundary metrics correlate strongly with mIoU on modern architectures, so the cone may almost never bind and the reform would be symbolic.
full_record.fastest_falsification_experiment: Inference-only scoring of 20 public MMSegmentation checkpoints on ADE20K val with mIoU and boundary-F takes under 6 hours on one GPU; all public.

one_line_idea: Cryptographic canary items for vision benchmarks: seeding test sets with arbitrary-labeled canary images gives benchmark hosts a statistically powered detector of training-on-test contamination that works as a protocol, not a forensic investigation.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Because canary labels are arbitrary (assigned by a keyed rule, not visual content), any above-chance canary accuracy is attributable to test-set exposure, so a small canary set embedded at benchmark creation yields a contamination test with quantifiable power and false-positive control, independent of model internals.

full_record.one_line_idea: Cryptographic canary items for vision benchmarks: seeding test sets with arbitrary-labeled canary images gives benchmark hosts a statistically powered detector of training-on-test contamination that works as a protocol, not a forensic investigation.
full_record.problem: [KNOWN FACT] Benchmark hosts cannot verify whether submitted models trained on test data; current contamination arguments rely on circumstantial evidence assembled long after the fact.
full_record.core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Because canary labels are arbitrary (assigned by a keyed rule, not visual content), any above-chance canary accuracy is attributable to test-set exposure, so a small canary set embedded at benchmark creation yields a contamination test with quantifiable power and false-positive control, independent of model internals.
full_record.falsifiable_prediction: [EXPECTED RESULT] With 200 canaries embedded in a benchmark, a model finetuned on a training set contaminated with the labeled test data will be detected at over 95% power at a 1% false-positive rate, while clean-trained models of any strength stay at chance on canaries; kill the idea if strong clean models exceed chance on canaries (visual-similarity leakage breaks arbitrariness) or if detection power at 200 canaries falls below 60%.
full_record.why_important: This is protocol-level infrastructure: it converts contamination disputes into a routine statistical check that benchmark hosts run at submission time, complementing mechanism-focused memorization research without overlapping it.
full_record.why_possibly_novel: [MODEL SPECULATION / unverified] Canary strings are established for language-model privacy auditing; a benchmark-side canary protocol for vision test-set contamination with power analysis appears undeveloped.
full_record.minimal_falsification_experiment: Construct a benchmark from ImageNet-subset classes plus 200 keyed-label canaries, finetune ViT-B and ResNet-50 (timm) under clean and deliberately contaminated regimes at several contamination fractions, and trace detection power versus canary count.
full_record.main_risk: Sophisticated contamination (training on test images without labels, or on near-duplicates) would evade label-keyed canaries, limiting the protocol to the crudest contamination mode.
full_record.community_default_belief: [MODEL SPECULATION] Contamination policing is assumed to require either data-pipeline transparency or post-hoc similarity forensics, both impractical at scale.
full_record.why_it_might_be_wrong: Public leaderboards may face mostly unlabeled-image contamination, for which this protocol is blind by design, making its deterrence value marginal.
full_record.fastest_falsification_experiment: A dozen short finetunes of timm ViT-B/ResNet-50 on ImageNet-100-scale subsets with injected canaries run in about 2 days total on one A100; all components public or scripted.

core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Inter-annotator agreement data (double-annotated subsets that several public datasets already ship) supports estimating a per-benchmark, per-class noise ceiling, and headroom-normalized reporting reorders both class-level priorities and model-level conclusions in the saturation regime.

full_record.one_line_idea: Noise-ceiling-normalized leaderboards: estimating each benchmark's inter-annotator ceiling and reporting scores as fractions of remaining headroom changes which improvements look meaningful, especially near saturation.
full_record.problem: [KNOWN FACT] Leaderboards report raw scores with no reference to the benchmark's annotation-noise ceiling, so a 0.5-point gain reads the same at 60% and at 95% of the achievable maximum.
full_record.core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Inter-annotator agreement data (double-annotated subsets that several public datasets already ship) supports estimating a per-benchmark, per-class noise ceiling, and headroom-normalized reporting reorders both class-level priorities and model-level conclusions in the saturation regime.
full_record.falsifiable_prediction: [EXPECTED RESULT] Using public double-annotation subsets to estimate ceilings on Cityscapes and LVIS, at least 20% of classes will show current best models within measurement noise of the ceiling (making further class gains unmeasurable), and headroom-normalized ranking will flip at least 1 of the top-3 model orderings on one benchmark; kill the idea if estimated ceilings exceed raw best scores by more than 10 points everywhere, meaning saturation is nowhere near and normalization changes nothing.
full_record.why_important: Prevents the community from spending compute on classes and benchmarks that are already measurement-limited and redirects it to real headroom, as a reporting capability rather than a critique.
full_record.why_possibly_novel: [MODEL SPECULATION / unverified] Noise ceilings are standard in neuroscience model evaluation; systematic ceiling-normalized reporting for vision benchmarks appears absent.
full_record.minimal_falsification_experiment: Estimate per-class ceilings from annotator-pair agreement on the double-annotated subsets, propagate uncertainty, and re-render public leaderboard slices (top-10 checkpoints) in headroom units with flip analysis.
full_record.main_risk: Double-annotated subsets are small and possibly unrepresentative, giving ceiling estimates with error bars wide enough to swallow the conclusions.
full_record.community_default_belief: [MODEL SPECULATION] Raw metric points are treated as having constant meaning across the score range, and saturation talk stays qualitative.
full_record.why_it_might_be_wrong: Model errors and annotator disagreements may be qualitatively different, so agreement-based estimates may not bound achievable model scores in either direction.
full_record.fastest_falsification_experiment: Ceiling estimation from public agreement subsets plus re-scoring 10 public checkpoints (MMSegmentation for Cityscapes, MMDetection for LVIS) is inference-plus-analysis, about 1 day on one GPU; all public.

one_line_idea: Difficulty-matched test refresh: replacing stale test images with fresh ones matched on anchor-model difficulty profiles preserves model rankings while breaking URL-level and hash-level contamination, enabling routine benchmark rotation.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] An image's difficulty profile (per-anchor-model scores across a frozen anchor ensemble) is a sufficient statistic for its effect on rankings, so sampling fresh images to match the joint difficulty-profile distribution of retired images yields a replacement set on which rankings and score levels are preserved for non-anchor models.

full_record.one_line_idea: Difficulty-matched test refresh: replacing stale test images with fresh ones matched on anchor-model difficulty profiles preserves model rankings while breaking URL-level and hash-level contamination, enabling routine benchmark rotation.
full_record.problem: [KNOWN FACT] Benchmarks cannot rotate their test sets without breaking comparability, because fresh images shift difficulty and invalidate historical numbers, so test sets stay static and contaminable for a decade.
full_record.core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] An image's difficulty profile (per-anchor-model scores across a frozen anchor ensemble) is a sufficient statistic for its effect on rankings, so sampling fresh images to match the joint difficulty-profile distribution of retired images yields a replacement set on which rankings and score levels are preserved for non-anchor models.
full_record.falsifiable_prediction: [EXPECTED RESULT] Swapping 50% of a COCO-classes evaluation set with difficulty-matched fresh images drawn from Open Images will preserve the ranking of 10 held-out public detectors with Kendall tau at least 0.9 and mean absolute score shift under 0.5 AP, versus tau under 0.8 for unmatched refresh; kill the idea if matched refresh does no better than unmatched or tau falls below 0.7.
full_record.why_important: Routine rotation is the strongest structural defense against test-set contamination and overfitting, and difficulty matching is the missing piece that keeps longitudinal comparability.
full_record.why_possibly_novel: [MODEL SPECULATION / unverified] Difficulty estimation per item exists; using anchor-profile matching to certify ranking-preserving test refresh appears untested.
full_record.minimal_falsification_experiment: Score anchor and held-out detector pools on COCO val2017 and a relabeled Open Images candidate pool, run matched and random 50% swaps, and compare ranking preservation and score-level drift across 20 refresh replicates.
full_record.main_risk: Cross-dataset label-convention differences between the source and refresh pools could dominate the swap effect, confounding the difficulty-matching evaluation.
full_record.community_default_belief: [MODEL SPECULATION] Test sets are treated as irreplaceable artifacts whose rotation necessarily resets all historical comparisons.
full_record.why_it_might_be_wrong: Difficulty profiles from anchors may not span the factors that differentiate future models, so preservation for today's held-out pool may not extend to tomorrow's architectures.
full_record.fastest_falsification_experiment: Inference of ~16 public MMDetection checkpoints on COCO val2017 and an Open Images subset with shared classes takes about 1 day on one GPU; both datasets and all models public.

one_line_idea: Partial-pooling estimators for rare-class metrics: hierarchical shrinkage of per-class AP/IoU stabilizes long-tail leaderboards, halving bootstrap rank volatility and changing which long-tail methods win.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Per-class scores share structure (class prototypes, frequency bands), so an empirical-Bayes partial-pooling estimator borrows strength across classes to produce rare-split estimates that are both lower-variance and better predictors of scores on a second sample, changing method comparisons that currently hinge on noise.

full_record.one_line_idea: Partial-pooling estimators for rare-class metrics: hierarchical shrinkage of per-class AP/IoU stabilizes long-tail leaderboards, halving bootstrap rank volatility and changing which long-tail methods win.
full_record.problem: [KNOWN FACT] Rare-class metrics on long-tail benchmarks rest on a handful of instances per class, so per-class scores and the rare-split averages built from them are wildly unstable, yet leaderboards report them as point values.
full_record.core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Per-class scores share structure (class prototypes, frequency bands), so an empirical-Bayes partial-pooling estimator borrows strength across classes to produce rare-split estimates that are both lower-variance and better predictors of scores on a second sample, changing method comparisons that currently hinge on noise.
full_record.falsifiable_prediction: [EXPECTED RESULT] On LVIS v1 val, partial-pooled rare-class AP will reduce bootstrap rank volatility among 6 public long-tail methods by at least a factor of 2 and will flip at least 1 published pairwise ordering; cross-validated prediction of held-out-split class scores will improve (lower MSE) for at least 80% of rare classes; kill the idea if volatility reduction is under 1.2x or held-out prediction does not improve.
full_record.why_important: Long-tail research currently optimizes against noise on the rare split; a stabilized estimator redirects the subfield toward real effects and is adoptable by the benchmark host directly.
full_record.why_possibly_novel: [MODEL SPECULATION / unverified] Empirical-Bayes shrinkage is classical; its application to long-tail vision leaderboards with a rank-stability and flip audit appears new.
full_record.minimal_falsification_experiment: Fit hierarchical models over per-class AP of 6 public LVIS checkpoints, compare raw vs pooled estimates under bootstrap resampling and split-half validation, and audit ordering flips on the rare split.
full_record.main_risk: Shrinkage pulls genuinely exceptional per-class performances toward the mean, and methods specializing on a few rare classes would be systematically under-credited.
full_record.community_default_belief: [MODEL SPECULATION] Per-class point estimates are treated as the honest raw data, with shrinkage viewed as statistical tampering.
full_record.why_it_might_be_wrong: If method effects on rare classes are strongly class-idiosyncratic, no pooling structure fits and the estimator's cross-validation advantage disappears.
full_record.fastest_falsification_experiment: Scoring 6 public LVIS checkpoints (MMDetection configs and the public Detic release) plus hierarchical fitting runs in about 8 hours on one GPU; all public.

one_line_idea: Boundary-affinity point supervision: growing instance masks from a 10-click-per-image budget through an affinity field trained only on click pairs reaches most of full-mask panoptic quality, because clicks constrain topology while affinities carry geometry.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] The residual gap is not information-theoretic but architectural: clicks uniquely identify instances (topology) while modern self-supervised features already encode boundary geometry, so a pairwise affinity head trained on click co-membership, decoded with a graph partitioner, converts 10 clicks into masks that capture most of what polygons supply.

full_record.one_line_idea: Boundary-affinity point supervision: growing instance masks from a 10-click-per-image budget through an affinity field trained only on click pairs reaches most of full-mask panoptic quality, because clicks constrain topology while affinities carry geometry.
full_record.problem: [KNOWN FACT] Full mask annotation costs about two orders of magnitude more than point clicks, yet point-supervised panoptic pipelines still trail full supervision by a wide margin.
full_record.core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] The residual gap is not information-theoretic but architectural: clicks uniquely identify instances (topology) while modern self-supervised features already encode boundary geometry, so a pairwise affinity head trained on click co-membership, decoded with a graph partitioner, converts 10 clicks into masks that capture most of what polygons supply.
full_record.falsifiable_prediction: [EXPECTED RESULT] On COCO panoptic with 10 simulated clicks per image, affinity-grown supervision will reach at least 88% of the full-mask-trained PQ of the same architecture, and at least +4 PQ over strongest point-loss-only baselines; kill the idea if it stays under 80% of full-mask PQ or within 1 PQ of point-loss baselines.
full_record.why_important: A validated 10-click protocol changes the economics of building new panoptic datasets and gives weak supervision a mechanism-level explanation of when clicks suffice.
full_record.why_possibly_novel: [MODEL SPECULATION / unverified] Point-supervised segmentation exists (point-based training losses); the explicit topology-vs-geometry decomposition with click-pair affinity training and a percentage-of-full-PQ kill line appears new.
full_record.minimal_falsification_experiment: Simulate click budgets on COCO panoptic, train a Mask2Former variant with click-pair affinity supervision on DINOv2 features vs point-loss baselines and full masks, and compare PQ at matched compute.
full_record.main_risk: Click simulation (uniform interior sampling) flatters the method relative to real annotator click distributions, which cluster near object centers and miss thin parts.
full_record.community_default_belief: [MODEL SPECULATION] Weak supervision is expected to trade large accuracy losses for cost, and points are seen as too impoverished for panoptic-quality masks.
full_record.why_it_might_be_wrong: Affinity fields may fail exactly on the classes where masks matter most (articulated, thin, overlapping objects), leaving the gap concentrated and unacceptable.
full_record.fastest_falsification_experiment: Three trainings (affinity, point-loss, full) of Mask2Former-R50 on COCO panoptic subsets take about 3 days total on one A100; COCO and DINOv2 are public.

one_line_idea: Box-plus-one-interior-point supervision: adding a single interior click to each box annotation closes more than half of the box-only-to-full-mask instance segmentation gap by resolving the figure-ground ambiguity that box supervision cannot.

one_line_idea: Scribble supervision with a topology-preserving connectivity loss recovers thin-structure segmentation (poles, fences, sign posts) that standard scribble training loses, at unchanged cost on thick classes.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Thin-class failure under scribbles is a connectivity problem, not a data-quantity problem: adding a differentiable connectivity/topology penalty that requires predicted thin-class components to connect scribble endpoints restores continuity, so most of the thin-class gap closes without any extra annotation.

full_record.one_line_idea: Scribble supervision with a topology-preserving connectivity loss recovers thin-structure segmentation (poles, fences, sign posts) that standard scribble training loses, at unchanged cost on thick classes.
full_record.problem: [KNOWN FACT] Scribble-supervised segmentation approaches full supervision on bulky classes but collapses on thin, elongated structures, whose continuity is exactly what pixel-wise losses fail to enforce from sparse scribbles.
full_record.core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Thin-class failure under scribbles is a connectivity problem, not a data-quantity problem: adding a differentiable connectivity/topology penalty that requires predicted thin-class components to connect scribble endpoints restores continuity, so most of the thin-class gap closes without any extra annotation.
full_record.falsifiable_prediction: [EXPECTED RESULT] On Cityscapes with simulated scribbles, adding the connectivity loss will recover at least 60% of the thin-class (pole, traffic sign pole, fence) IoU gap between scribble and full supervision while changing thick-class IoU by under 0.5; kill the idea if thin-class gap recovery is under 25% or thick classes degrade by over 1.0 IoU.
full_record.why_important: Thin structures carry outsized downstream importance (infrastructure inspection, driving) and are the acknowledged weak point of every cheap-supervision protocol; a targeted repair makes scribbles viable end-to-end.
full_record.why_possibly_novel: [MODEL SPECULATION / unverified] Topology-aware losses exist for full supervision in specialized pipelines; coupling them to scribble endpoints as a weak-supervision repair with a gap-recovery kill line appears new.
full_record.minimal_falsification_experiment: Generate skeleton-based scribbles for Cityscapes, train DeepLabv3+ with and without the connectivity penalty, and report per-class IoU deltas stratified by structure thinness.
full_record.main_risk: Differentiable topology penalties are computationally heavy and unstable at high resolution, and a proxy (e.g., skeleton-overlap loss) may weaken the mechanism claim.
full_record.community_default_belief: [MODEL SPECULATION] Thin-class failure is filed under insufficient supervision, with the assumed fix being more or denser annotation rather than a structural loss.
full_record.why_it_might_be_wrong: Thin-class failure may be dominated by feature-resolution limits of the backbone, in which case no loss on top of the same features can restore continuity.
full_record.fastest_falsification_experiment: Two DeepLabv3+ trainings on Cityscapes (MMSegmentation) plus scribble generation run in about 1.5 days on one A100; data and models public.

one_line_idea: Complement-masked training for disjointly labeled dataset unions: masking the loss over classes a source did not label, plus cross-image class banks, trains one model from three partially labeled datasets to near fully-labeled-union quality.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] The union-training failure is a supervision-semantics bug, not a data limitation: treating unlabeled classes as ignore (complement masking) removes the false-negative gradients, and a class-bank memory that replays confident cross-dataset features restores the missing positive signal, together recovering nearly all of the fully-labeled-union performance.

full_record.one_line_idea: Complement-masked training for disjointly labeled dataset unions: masking the loss over classes a source did not label, plus cross-image class banks, trains one model from three partially labeled datasets to near fully-labeled-union quality.
full_record.problem: [KNOWN FACT] Real datasets label different class subsets (driving sets lack indoor classes and vice versa), and naive union training punishes correct predictions of classes the current source treats as background.
full_record.core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] The union-training failure is a supervision-semantics bug, not a data limitation: treating unlabeled classes as ignore (complement masking) removes the false-negative gradients, and a class-bank memory that replays confident cross-dataset features restores the missing positive signal, together recovering nearly all of the fully-labeled-union performance.
full_record.falsifiable_prediction: [EXPECTED RESULT] Splitting ADE20K classes into three disjoint label groups across three sub-datasets, complement masking plus class banks will train a model within 2.0 mIoU of the fully-labeled-union reference, versus a naive-union baseline at least 8 mIoU below it; kill the idea if the method stays more than 5 mIoU below the reference, meaning partial labeling loses irrecoverable information.
full_record.why_important: A validated recipe for disjoint-label unions unlocks training on the union of existing public datasets without any re-annotation, one of the cheapest data-scaling moves available.
full_record.why_possibly_novel: [MODEL SPECULATION / unverified] Partial-label semantics and cross-dataset training have been studied piecemeal; a controlled disjoint-split benchmark with a recovery-gap kill line appears missing.
full_record.minimal_falsification_experiment: Create the controlled three-way split of ADE20K, train naive-union, complement-masked, masked-plus-bank, and full-union references with SegFormer, and compare mIoU and per-group breakdowns.
full_record.main_risk: Class banks rely on confident pseudo-features whose errors could compound for visually similar cross-group classes, capping recovery below the target.
full_record.community_default_belief: [MODEL SPECULATION] Practitioners assume datasets with different label spaces cannot be merged without relabeling or per-dataset heads.
full_record.why_it_might_be_wrong: Context co-occurrence across groups may be irreplaceable: without seeing labeled sofa and labeled wall in the same image, boundary discrimination between them may never form.
full_record.fastest_falsification_experiment: Four SegFormer-B0 trainings on ADE20K splits take about 2 days total on one A100; ADE20K and SegFormer are public.

one_line_idea: A clicks-to-quality scaling law: interactive annotation quality follows a power law in click budget whose exponent is shared across datasets and interfaces, enabling annotation-budget planning from a 50-image pilot.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Achieved mask quality as a function of interaction budget follows a saturating power law whose exponent reflects boundary complexity statistics that are broadly shared across natural-image datasets, so a small pilot suffices to fit the curve and predict the budget needed for any target quality on a new dataset.

full_record.one_line_idea: A clicks-to-quality scaling law: interactive annotation quality follows a power law in click budget whose exponent is shared across datasets and interfaces, enabling annotation-budget planning from a 50-image pilot.
full_record.problem: [KNOWN FACT] Annotation campaigns set click and time budgets by folklore, with no quantitative law connecting per-instance interaction budget to achieved label quality across datasets.
full_record.core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Achieved mask quality as a function of interaction budget follows a saturating power law whose exponent reflects boundary complexity statistics that are broadly shared across natural-image datasets, so a small pilot suffices to fit the curve and predict the budget needed for any target quality on a new dataset.
full_record.falsifiable_prediction: [EXPECTED RESULT] Fitting the law on 50-image pilots from COCO and ADE20K (simulated interaction via public interactive-segmentation models) will predict the full clicks-to-IoU curve on Cityscapes and Pascal VOC within 5% quality error across budgets of 1-20 clicks; kill the idea if cross-dataset prediction error exceeds 15% or if fitted exponents differ across datasets by more than a factor of 2, breaking the shared-exponent claim.
full_record.why_important: Turns annotation budgeting into measurement: a lab can decide clicks-per-instance and campaign cost from a one-afternoon pilot instead of guesswork.
full_record.why_possibly_novel: [MODEL SPECULATION / unverified] Interactive segmentation papers report clicks-to-IoU curves per method; treating the curve as a transferable dataset law with pilot-based extrapolation appears new.
full_record.minimal_falsification_experiment: Run a public interactive segmentation model (SimpleClick or RITM) with simulated user policies across click budgets on four datasets, fit the power law per dataset, and test pilot-to-full and cross-dataset extrapolation.
full_record.main_risk: Simulated clicking underestimates human variability, so the law may hold for robot users but fail for real annotator populations.
full_record.community_default_belief: [MODEL SPECULATION] Clicks-to-quality behavior is assumed method-specific and dataset-specific, not law-like or transferable.
full_record.why_it_might_be_wrong: Boundary-complexity distributions may differ enough across domains (driving vs indoor) that no shared exponent exists even approximately.
full_record.fastest_falsification_experiment: Simulated interactive annotation with the public SimpleClick checkpoint over subsets of COCO, ADE20K, Cityscapes, and VOC runs in under 8 hours on one consumer GPU; all public.

one_line_idea: Train-time depth as free boundary supervision: distilling depth-discontinuity and normal-discontinuity maps from RGB-D training data into a 2D segmentation model improves boundary quality with zero test-time depth requirement.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Boundary supervision is the scarcest part of the segmentation signal, and depth/normal discontinuities provide a dense, annotation-free boundary teacher; an auxiliary boundary-distillation loss from train-time depth therefore improves boundary-F on RGB-only inference more than equivalent-compute image-only auxiliary losses.

full_record.one_line_idea: Train-time depth as free boundary supervision: distilling depth-discontinuity and normal-discontinuity maps from RGB-D training data into a 2D segmentation model improves boundary quality with zero test-time depth requirement.
full_record.problem: [KNOWN FACT] Public RGB-D datasets carry precise geometric discontinuities that align with object boundaries, yet 2D segmentation training typically ignores the depth channel even when it is available at training time.
full_record.core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Boundary supervision is the scarcest part of the segmentation signal, and depth/normal discontinuities provide a dense, annotation-free boundary teacher; an auxiliary boundary-distillation loss from train-time depth therefore improves boundary-F on RGB-only inference more than equivalent-compute image-only auxiliary losses.
full_record.falsifiable_prediction: [EXPECTED RESULT] On NYUv2 (RGB-only at test), depth-discontinuity distillation will improve boundary-F by at least 3.0 points and mIoU by at least 1.0 over the no-auxiliary baseline, and by at least 1.5 boundary-F over an edge-detector-distillation control at matched compute; kill the idea if it fails to beat the edge-distillation control by 0.5 boundary-F, meaning geometry adds nothing beyond photometric edges.
full_record.why_important: Recasts existing RGB-D archives as free supervision for ordinary 2D models, a capability claim about supervision sources rather than architectures, with a control that isolates the geometric contribution.
full_record.why_possibly_novel: [MODEL SPECULATION / unverified] Depth-aware segmentation typically consumes depth at test time; train-only geometric-boundary distillation with a photometric-edge control appears under-examined.
full_record.minimal_falsification_experiment: Train SegFormer on NYUv2 RGB with (a) no auxiliary, (b) edge-distillation from a public edge detector, (c) depth-discontinuity distillation from the dataset's depth channel, and compare boundary-F/mIoU; replicate on SUN RGB-D.
full_record.main_risk: Sensor depth is noisy at exactly the thin structures where boundary supervision matters, potentially teaching the model sensor artifacts.
full_record.community_default_belief: [MODEL SPECULATION] Depth is treated as a test-time modality choice, not as a train-time supervision source for RGB-only models.
full_record.why_it_might_be_wrong: Photometric edges may already contain the usable boundary signal, with geometric edges adding only redundancy that matched-compute controls will expose.
full_record.fastest_falsification_experiment: Three SegFormer-B0 trainings on NYUv2 take under 1 day total on one consumer GPU; NYUv2, SUN RGB-D, and public edge detectors are all public.

one_line_idea: One-exemplar dataset bootstrapping: a single annotated exemplar per class, propagated through frozen-feature retrieval and geometric verification, generates pseudo-labels sufficient to train a segmentation model to a large fraction of full supervision.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Frozen self-supervised features make one careful exemplar per class a viable teacher: dense retrieval finds visually corresponding regions across the unlabeled corpus, geometric verification (cycle-consistent matching) filters false positives, and the surviving pseudo-labels carry enough signal that standard training recovers most of full-supervision quality for medium-frequency classes.

full_record.one_line_idea: One-exemplar dataset bootstrapping: a single annotated exemplar per class, propagated through frozen-feature retrieval and geometric verification, generates pseudo-labels sufficient to train a segmentation model to a large fraction of full supervision.
full_record.problem: [KNOWN FACT] Bootstrapping a new segmentation dataset currently starts from hundreds of labeled images per class, because pseudo-labeling pipelines need a trained teacher to begin with.
full_record.core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Frozen self-supervised features make one careful exemplar per class a viable teacher: dense retrieval finds visually corresponding regions across the unlabeled corpus, geometric verification (cycle-consistent matching) filters false positives, and the surviving pseudo-labels carry enough signal that standard training recovers most of full-supervision quality for medium-frequency classes.
full_record.falsifiable_prediction: [EXPECTED RESULT] On Pascal VOC with 1 exemplar mask per class and 10k unlabeled images, the bootstrap will train a model to at least 60% of full-supervision mIoU, with cycle-consistency filtering contributing at least 10 mIoU over unfiltered retrieval; kill the idea if final quality is under 40% of full supervision or filtering contributes under 3 mIoU.
full_record.why_important: Reduces the cold-start cost of new dense-prediction domains to one annotation per class plus compute, and quantifies which mechanism (retrieval vs verification) carries the capability.
full_record.why_possibly_novel: [MODEL SPECULATION / unverified] Few-shot segmentation and retrieval-based propagation exist; an end-to-end one-exemplar dataset-bootstrap protocol with a filtering-ablation kill line appears new.
full_record.minimal_falsification_experiment: Select exemplars, run DINOv2 dense retrieval plus cycle verification over the VOC trainaug pool, train DeepLabv3+ on the pseudo-labels, and ablate the verification stage.
full_record.main_risk: Single exemplars encode one pose/context, so classes with high intra-class variation (chairs, plants) may bootstrap poorly, concentrating failure where data is most needed.
full_record.community_default_belief: [MODEL SPECULATION] Useful pseudo-labeling is assumed to require a supervised teacher trained on substantial labeled data.
full_record.why_it_might_be_wrong: Retrieval precision may collapse for stuff-like or deformable classes, and no geometric verification can rescue retrieval that finds the wrong objects.
full_record.fastest_falsification_experiment: DINOv2 retrieval over 10k images plus two DeepLabv3+ trainings completes in about 1.5 days on one consumer GPU; VOC/SBD and DINOv2 are public.
