one_line_idea: Verified negatives are the high-value half of weak supervision: human-verified negative image-level labels (already shipped in Open Images) improve weakly supervised detection more per label than an equal number of extra positives.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] The dominant error source in weak detection training is corrupted negative evidence (classes assumed absent that are actually present), so explicitly verified negatives repair the loss where it is most wrong, delivering more AP per label than additional positives, which mostly duplicate existing evidence.

full_record.one_line_idea: Verified negatives are the high-value half of weak supervision: human-verified negative image-level labels (already shipped in Open Images) improve weakly supervised detection more per label than an equal number of extra positives.
full_record.problem: [KNOWN FACT] Open Images ships millions of human-verified negative image-level labels alongside positives, but weakly supervised detection research consumes positives and treats negatives as incidental.
full_record.core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] The dominant error source in weak detection training is corrupted negative evidence (classes assumed absent that are actually present), so explicitly verified negatives repair the loss where it is most wrong, delivering more AP per label than additional positives, which mostly duplicate existing evidence.
full_record.falsifiable_prediction: [EXPECTED RESULT] In matched-label-count experiments on Open Images subsets, adding N verified negatives will improve weakly supervised detection AP by at least 2x the gain from adding N extra verified positives, with at least +3.0 AP absolute at N equal to one negative per training image; kill the idea if the per-label value ratio falls below 1.2x, meaning negatives are not preferentially valuable.
full_record.why_important: Reprices an already-existing, underused public resource and gives annotation campaigns a measured reason to buy cheap emptiness judgments alongside positives.
full_record.why_possibly_novel: [MODEL SPECULATION / unverified] Verified negatives are used internally by some pipelines; a controlled per-label marginal-value comparison of negatives vs positives for weak detection appears unreported.
full_record.minimal_falsification_experiment: Train a weakly supervised detector on Open Images image-level labels with (a) positives only, (b) positives + N verified negatives, (c) positives + N extra positives, at matched label budgets, and compare AP on the Open Images detection validation split.
full_record.main_risk: Verified negatives in Open Images are non-uniformly sampled (verification followed model uncertainty), so their measured value may not transfer to fresh annotation campaigns.
full_record.community_default_belief: [MODEL SPECULATION] Weak-supervision value is assumed to live in positive labels, negatives being effectively free from absence.
full_record.why_it_might_be_wrong: Modern weak-detection losses with noise modeling may already discount unverified negatives well enough that explicit verification adds little.
full_record.fastest_falsification_experiment: Three weakly supervised detection trainings on a 100k-image Open Images subset (WSDDN-style or a modern reimplementation) run in about 2.5 days total on one A100; dataset and baseline code public.

one_line_idea: Budget-optimal supervision mixing: a cost-model-driven allocator that chooses per-image supervision grade (clicks, boxes, or masks) from image statistics beats any single-grade budget spend on final model quality.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] The information value of upgrading an image from boxes to masks is predictable from cheap image statistics (instance count, boundary complexity, class rarity), so a greedy allocator that spends a fixed budget where upgrade value is highest dominates uniform single-grade allocations on the trained model's quality.

full_record.one_line_idea: Budget-optimal supervision mixing: a cost-model-driven allocator that chooses per-image supervision grade (clicks, boxes, or masks) from image statistics beats any single-grade budget spend on final model quality.
full_record.problem: [KNOWN FACT] Annotation campaigns choose one supervision grade for a whole dataset, even though per-image difficulty and per-grade information value vary enormously across images.
full_record.core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] The information value of upgrading an image from boxes to masks is predictable from cheap image statistics (instance count, boundary complexity, class rarity), so a greedy allocator that spends a fixed budget where upgrade value is highest dominates uniform single-grade allocations on the trained model's quality.
full_record.falsifiable_prediction: [EXPECTED RESULT] On COCO with simulated costs (masks 8x boxes, boxes 5x clicks), the allocator's mixed portfolio will beat the best single-grade allocation at equal budget by at least 2.0 mask-AP, and a value-model ablation (random mixing at the same grade proportions) will capture under half the gain; kill the idea if the allocator beats the best single grade by under 0.5 mask-AP, meaning mixing has no exploitable structure.
full_record.why_important: Converts supervision-grade choice from a policy decision into an optimization, directly reducing the cost of every future dense-prediction dataset.
full_record.why_possibly_novel: [MODEL SPECULATION / unverified] Mixed-supervision training methods exist; a budgeted allocation policy with a validated per-image value model and matched-budget dominance test appears new.
full_record.minimal_falsification_experiment: Simulate grade costs on COCO, train models under single-grade and allocator-chosen mixed portfolios at three budgets using existing mixed-supervision losses, and compare mask-AP frontiers with the random-mixing control.
full_record.main_risk: The value model is fitted on proxy runs whose transfer across architectures is unproven; a value model that overfits one architecture family would undermine the general claim.
full_record.community_default_belief: [MODEL SPECULATION] Supervision-grade uniformity is assumed operationally necessary and near-optimal, with mixing seen as tooling complexity for marginal benefit.
full_record.why_it_might_be_wrong: Under matched budget the extra images affordable at lower grades may always dominate the precision of fewer high-grade labels, collapsing the optimum to a single grade after all.
full_record.fastest_falsification_experiment: About eight Mask R-CNN trainings on COCO subsets (MMDetection) across budgets and portfolios take roughly 5 single-A100 days; COCO and mixed-supervision baseline code are public.

one_line_idea: Occlusion-order supervision is sufficient for amodal completion: training with only pairwise over/under relations (free from existing overlap annotations) yields amodal masks competitive with fully amodal-supervised training.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] The hard part of amodal completion is knowing which regions are occluded rather than hallucinating shape: pairwise occlusion-order labels identify the occluded support, and generic class shape priors fill it, so order supervision plus modal masks recovers most of what explicit amodal masks teach.

full_record.one_line_idea: Occlusion-order supervision is sufficient for amodal completion: training with only pairwise over/under relations (free from existing overlap annotations) yields amodal masks competitive with fully amodal-supervised training.
full_record.problem: [KNOWN FACT] Amodal segmentation datasets are rare and expensive because annotators must imagine hidden object extents, while ordinary datasets contain abundant implicit occlusion evidence (overlapping instances with depth order).
full_record.core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] The hard part of amodal completion is knowing which regions are occluded rather than hallucinating shape: pairwise occlusion-order labels identify the occluded support, and generic class shape priors fill it, so order supervision plus modal masks recovers most of what explicit amodal masks teach.
full_record.falsifiable_prediction: [EXPECTED RESULT] On KINS, a model trained with modal masks plus occlusion-order labels only will reach at least 80% of the amodal mask-AP of a fully amodal-supervised twin, and beat a modal-finetune baseline by at least 5 amodal AP; kill the idea if it reaches under 60% of the supervised twin, meaning explicit amodal extent labels carry irreplaceable information.
full_record.why_important: If order labels suffice, amodal capability can be added to any instance dataset for a fraction of amodal-annotation cost, unlocking occlusion-robust downstream use broadly.
full_record.why_possibly_novel: [MODEL SPECULATION / unverified] Amodal methods typically train on amodal masks; a controlled sufficiency test of order-plus-modal supervision with a percentage-of-supervised kill line appears new.
full_record.minimal_falsification_experiment: Train three variants (modal-only, modal+order, fully amodal) of the same amodal head on KINS and COCOA, evaluating amodal AP and stratifying by occlusion severity.
full_record.main_risk: Shape priors may carry most of the signal for rigid vehicle classes in KINS, flattering the method in one domain and hiding failures on deformable categories.
full_record.community_default_belief: [MODEL SPECULATION] Amodal completion is assumed to require amodal ground truth; order relations are treated as auxiliary metadata.
full_record.why_it_might_be_wrong: Occluded-extent prediction may depend on instance-specific evidence (pose, articulation) that order labels do not constrain, capping recovery below usefulness.
full_record.fastest_falsification_experiment: Three trainings of a Mask R-CNN-based amodal head on KINS (public, KITTI-derived) take about 1.5 days total on one A100; KINS, COCOA, and Detectron2 are public.

one_line_idea: Amodal-extent anchor assignment: assigning training targets by estimated full-object extent instead of visible-box overlap recovers detections of heavily occluded objects that visible-IoU assignment systematically starves of positive anchors.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] The occlusion performance gap is partly a label-assignment artifact: using amodal extents (from annotation or a completion model) for assignment gives occluded objects a fair share of positive anchors, improving occluded-slice recall without harming visible-object precision, because the assignment change only adds positives where evidence exists.

full_record.one_line_idea: Amodal-extent anchor assignment: assigning training targets by estimated full-object extent instead of visible-box overlap recovers detections of heavily occluded objects that visible-IoU assignment systematically starves of positive anchors.
full_record.problem: [KNOWN FACT] Detector training assigns positives by IoU with the visible box, so heavily occluded objects receive few or no positive anchors and are undertrained precisely where detection is hardest.
full_record.core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] The occlusion performance gap is partly a label-assignment artifact: using amodal extents (from annotation or a completion model) for assignment gives occluded objects a fair share of positive anchors, improving occluded-slice recall without harming visible-object precision, because the assignment change only adds positives where evidence exists.
full_record.falsifiable_prediction: [EXPECTED RESULT] On KINS, amodal-extent assignment will improve AP on the over-50%-occluded slice by at least 2.0 points with under 0.3 overall AP change, and the gain will correlate with the increase in positive-anchor counts per occluded instance; kill the idea if the occluded-slice gain is under 0.5 AP, meaning assignment starvation is not a binding constraint.
full_record.why_important: Locates a concrete, fixable training mechanism behind the well-documented occlusion weakness of detectors, and the fix is a few lines in the assigner rather than a new architecture.
full_record.why_possibly_novel: [MODEL SPECULATION / unverified] Occlusion-robust detection work focuses on losses and NMS; amodal-extent-based label assignment with an anchor-count mediation analysis appears new.
full_record.minimal_falsification_experiment: Modify the assigner of Faster R-CNN and FCOS to use amodal boxes on KINS, train matched pairs, and report occluded-slice AP plus the mediation analysis on anchor counts.
full_record.main_risk: Amodal boxes overlap neighboring objects heavily, so added positives may inject label confusion between occluder and occludee, trading one error for another.
full_record.community_default_belief: [MODEL SPECULATION] Occlusion failures are attributed to representation limits, with label assignment assumed neutral.
full_record.why_it_might_be_wrong: Occluded instances may lack the visible evidence to exploit extra positives, so anchors were never the bottleneck.
full_record.fastest_falsification_experiment: Four detector trainings on KINS (public) with MMDetection take about 2 single-A100 days; all data and models public.

core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Occlusion robustness is learned progressively: presenting composited occlusions in a curriculum from light to heavy overlap (with consistent order geometry) lets the model build visible-evidence-to-extent associations stage by stage, so curriculum ordering, not paste volume, drives occluded-slice gains.

full_record.one_line_idea: Occlusion-graded curriculum by real-segment compositing: pasting real instance segments with progressively increasing overlap teaches occlusion robustness that random-paste augmentation misses, at identical augmentation budget.
full_record.problem: [KNOWN FACT] Copy-paste augmentation with real segments improves instance segmentation broadly, but its occlusion parameters (overlap fraction, ordering statistics) are left random, and models remain weak on heavy occlusion.
full_record.core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Occlusion robustness is learned progressively: presenting composited occlusions in a curriculum from light to heavy overlap (with consistent order geometry) lets the model build visible-evidence-to-extent associations stage by stage, so curriculum ordering, not paste volume, drives occluded-slice gains.
full_record.falsifiable_prediction: [EXPECTED RESULT] At matched paste counts on COCO, occlusion-graded curriculum will beat random-overlap pasting by at least 2.0 AP on the heavily occluded evaluation slice (defined via COCOA overlap statistics) while matching it within 0.3 AP overall; kill the idea if the curriculum's occluded-slice advantage is under 0.5 AP, meaning ordering carries no signal beyond exposure.
full_record.why_important: Upgrades the most widely adopted augmentation for instance tasks with a mechanism-specific schedule, and the curriculum-vs-exposure contrast cleanly tests whether ordering matters.
full_record.why_possibly_novel: [MODEL SPECULATION / unverified] Copy-paste augmentation is established; controlling and scheduling its occlusion statistics as the manipulated variable appears unexamined.
full_record.minimal_falsification_experiment: Implement overlap-controlled pasting on COCO, train Mask R-CNN under random vs graded schedules at matched budgets, and evaluate on occlusion-stratified slices of COCO val and COCOA.
full_record.main_risk: Composited occlusions lack contact shadows and depth-consistent lighting, so gains may not transfer to natural heavy occlusion.
full_record.community_default_belief: [MODEL SPECULATION] Copy-paste is treated as a volume knob whose internal statistics are second-order details.
full_record.why_it_might_be_wrong: Curriculum effects in vision training are often washed out by long schedules, and final performance may depend only on the stationary paste distribution.
full_record.fastest_falsification_experiment: Two Mask R-CNN trainings on COCO (MMDetection, 1x schedule) with scripted paste control take about 2 single-A100 days; COCO and COCOA are public. Scope note: this manipulates real-segment compositing statistics, not generative synthetic data.

core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Contextual object priors (co-occurrence, support surfaces, partial arrangements) carry enough information that a model trained on real images with instances deliberately occluded by pasted occluders learns above-chance hidden-object proposal, and this capability transfers to naturally occluded scenes rather than exploiting compositing artifacts.

full_record.one_line_idea: Context-driven proposal of fully hidden objects: a detector head trained on synthetic full-occlusion composites learns to propose completely invisible objects from scene context at usable precision, a capability absent from every current detector.
full_record.problem: [KNOWN FACT] Detectors only report objects with visible evidence, yet scenes contain strong contextual evidence for hidden objects (a mug fully behind a cereal box on a breakfast table), and no benchmark or capability exists for proposing them.
full_record.core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Contextual object priors (co-occurrence, support surfaces, partial arrangements) carry enough information that a model trained on real images with instances deliberately occluded by pasted occluders learns above-chance hidden-object proposal, and this capability transfers to naturally occluded scenes rather than exploiting compositing artifacts.
full_record.falsifiable_prediction: [EXPECTED RESULT] On a held-out benchmark built by fully covering annotated COCO instances with pasted occluders, the context head will achieve at least 30% recall of hidden objects at 3x the precision of a class-prior baseline (proposing frequent classes everywhere), and at least half of that precision advantage will survive on a small natural-occlusion probe set; kill the idea if recall at that precision is under 10% or if the advantage vanishes on natural scenes (artifact exploitation).
full_record.why_important: Establishes a new, measurable perception capability (object permanence from context in stills) with direct value for robotics and search applications, framed constructively rather than as a failure audit.
full_record.why_possibly_novel: [MODEL SPECULATION / unverified] Context modeling for detection is old, but a trained-and-benchmarked hidden-object proposal capability with an artifact-control kill clause appears new.
full_record.minimal_falsification_experiment: Construct the full-occlusion benchmark from COCO with controlled compositing, train a DETR-based context head, evaluate hidden-object recall/precision against class-prior and scene-retrieval baselines, and validate on a hand-verified natural-occlusion probe subset.
full_record.main_risk: The head may key on compositing cues (boundary sharpness, lighting mismatch) rather than context; the natural-probe control mitigates but cannot fully exclude this.
full_record.community_default_belief: [MODEL SPECULATION] Detection is defined over visible evidence, and proposing invisible objects is considered out of scope or unprincipled.
full_record.why_it_might_be_wrong: Contextual priors may be too diffuse in natural scenes: many objects could be behind the box, so precision at fixed recall may never clear the baseline meaningfully.
full_record.fastest_falsification_experiment: Benchmark construction and one DETR-head finetuning on COCO composites run in about 2 days on one A100; COCO and DETR are public.

full_record.why_important: A transfer-positive result licenses a universal amodal module usable on any dataset without amodal labels, multiplying the value of the few existing amodal annotations.
full_record.why_possibly_novel: [MODEL SPECULATION / unverified] Amodal papers report within-dataset results; a category-held-out transfer quantification with a retention kill line appears new.

full_record.main_risk: KINS's rigid, road-scene shapes may teach continuation priors that actively mislead on articulated or deformable held-out categories.
full_record.community_default_belief: [MODEL SPECULATION] Amodal completion is assumed to lean on category shape knowledge, implying poor novel-category transfer.
full_record.why_it_might_be_wrong: The measured retention may be dominated by trivially easy small occlusions, overstating generic skill; occlusion-severity stratification is needed to expose this.

one_line_idea: Layered panoptic decoding: representing the scene as depth-ordered mask layers instead of a flat label map fixes boundary-ownership errors between overlapping instances, improving contested-boundary accuracy at equal overall quality.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Boundary ownership is a layering question: decoding into ordered layers (each instance keeps a complete mask in its layer, flattened by learned order) lets the model represent the occlusion relation explicitly, converting ownership conflicts into order decisions it can learn, so contested-boundary errors drop without any backbone change.

full_record.one_line_idea: Layered panoptic decoding: representing the scene as depth-ordered mask layers instead of a flat label map fixes boundary-ownership errors between overlapping instances, improving contested-boundary accuracy at equal overall quality.
full_record.problem: [KNOWN FACT] Panoptic decoders emit one flat label per pixel, forcing overlapping instances to compete for boundary pixels, and boundary-ownership errors between adjacent overlapping objects are a persistent error mode.
full_record.core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Boundary ownership is a layering question: decoding into ordered layers (each instance keeps a complete mask in its layer, flattened by learned order) lets the model represent the occlusion relation explicitly, converting ownership conflicts into order decisions it can learn, so contested-boundary errors drop without any backbone change.
full_record.falsifiable_prediction: [EXPECTED RESULT] On COCO panoptic, layered decoding will reduce boundary-ownership error (misassigned boundary-band pixels between overlapping instance pairs) by at least 25% relative and improve boundary-F on contested bands by at least 2.0 points, at overall PQ within 0.3 of the flat decoder; kill the idea if contested-band improvement is under 8% relative or PQ drops by more than 1.0.
full_record.why_important: Boundary ownership drives downstream failures in editing and robotics grasping; a decoding-level repair that needs no new labels is immediately deployable on existing panoptic stacks.
full_record.why_possibly_novel: [MODEL SPECULATION / unverified] Layered scene representations are classical and appear in image editing; wiring them into panoptic decoding with a contested-band error metric and kill line appears new.
full_record.minimal_falsification_experiment: Add a layer-ordered decoding path to Mask2Former panoptic, train matched pairs on COCO panoptic, and evaluate the contested-band metrics computed from overlapping ground-truth pairs.
full_record.main_risk: Layer count and order supervision (from mask overlap heuristics) introduce new hyperparameters whose tuning could account for any observed gains.
full_record.community_default_belief: [MODEL SPECULATION] Flat per-pixel labeling is treated as the natural output space for panoptic tasks, with ownership errors accepted as annotation-level ambiguity.
full_record.why_it_might_be_wrong: The ownership errors may originate in feature resolution rather than output-space expressiveness, in which case layering changes nothing measurable.
full_record.fastest_falsification_experiment: Two Mask2Former-R50 panoptic trainings on COCO take about 2.5 days total on one A100; COCO panoptic and Mask2Former are public.

one_line_idea: Backbone-portable feature upsamplers: a high-resolution feature upsampler trained once on one frozen backbone transfers to other backbones with most of its dense-task benefit intact, so upsampling can ship as a universal plug-in rather than a per-model accessory.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] The information an upsampler exploits is dominated by image-side statistics (edge-guided detail reconstruction) rather than backbone-specific feature idiosyncrasies, so an upsampler trained on backbone A composes with backbone B after only a cheap linear input adapter, retaining most of the dense-task gain.

full_record.one_line_idea: Backbone-portable feature upsamplers: a high-resolution feature upsampler trained once on one frozen backbone transfers to other backbones with most of its dense-task benefit intact, so upsampling can ship as a universal plug-in rather than a per-model accessory.
full_record.problem: [KNOWN FACT] Frozen vision backbones emit coarse feature grids (stride 14-16), and learned upsamplers that restore spatial detail (FeatUp lineage) are trained per backbone, multiplying cost across the model zoo.
full_record.core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] The information an upsampler exploits is dominated by image-side statistics (edge-guided detail reconstruction) rather than backbone-specific feature idiosyncrasies, so an upsampler trained on backbone A composes with backbone B after only a cheap linear input adapter, retaining most of the dense-task gain.
full_record.falsifiable_prediction: [EXPECTED RESULT] An upsampler trained on frozen DINOv2 and transferred to OpenCLIP ViT-B with a linear adapter fitted on 1k unlabeled images will retain at least 75% of the linear-probe segmentation mIoU gain it delivers on its home backbone (measured on ADE20K over bilinear upsampling); kill the idea if retention is under 40%, meaning upsamplers are backbone-specific artifacts.
full_record.why_important: A portable upsampler makes high-resolution dense readout a commodity component, cutting the per-backbone retraining tax and clarifying what upsamplers actually learn.
full_record.why_possibly_novel: [MODEL SPECULATION / unverified] Learned feature upsampling is established (FeatUp lineage); its cross-backbone portability with an adapter-only transfer protocol appears untested. Scope note: this concerns feature-space readout for dense prediction, not image super-resolution or restoration.
full_record.minimal_falsification_experiment: Train the upsampler on DINOv2, freeze it, fit linear adapters to OpenCLIP and a supervised ViT, and compare ADE20K/VOC linear-probe mIoU with home-trained upsamplers, bilinear, and adapter-only controls.
full_record.main_risk: Feature-space geometry may differ enough across pretraining objectives that a linear adapter cannot align what the upsampler needs, forcing nonlinear adapters that blur the portability claim.
full_record.community_default_belief: [MODEL SPECULATION] Upsamplers are assumed to be backbone-married components retrained per model as a matter of course.
full_record.why_it_might_be_wrong: The gain retention may be dominated by trivial edge alignment achievable by guided filtering, making the portability finding true but practically empty against cheap baselines.
full_record.fastest_falsification_experiment: Upsampler training plus adapter fits and linear-probe evaluations on ADE20K with public DINOv2/OpenCLIP checkpoints run in about 1.5 days on one consumer GPU; all public.

full_record.one_line_idea: Implicit coordinate-based dense readout beats deconvolutional heads at matched compute on boundary accuracy, because continuous decoding removes the grid-aliasing that upsampling stacks bake into predictions.
full_record.problem: [KNOWN FACT] Dense heads reconstruct full-resolution predictions through fixed upsampling stacks whose outputs show grid-aligned artifacts, and boundary quality lags region quality across architectures.
full_record.core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] A coordinate-conditioned implicit head (query any continuous location against local feature neighborhoods) eliminates resampling alias by construction, so at matched compute it converts the same features into sharper boundaries, with the advantage growing at evaluation resolutions above training resolution.
full_record.falsifiable_prediction: [EXPECTED RESULT] On ADE20K with a frozen DINOv2 backbone, the implicit head will beat a parameter-matched deconv head by at least 2.0 boundary-F at equal mIoU (within 0.3), and the boundary-F advantage will at least double when evaluating at 2x training resolution; kill the idea if the boundary-F advantage is under 0.5 at native resolution and does not grow with resolution.
full_record.why_important: Locates a persistent boundary-quality pathology in the readout stage rather than the representation, and offers a drop-in head that any frozen-backbone user can adopt.
full_record.why_possibly_novel: [MODEL SPECULATION / unverified] Implicit decoding heads exist in scattered forms (point-based refinement, implicit fields); the matched-compute aliasing-attribution comparison with a resolution-scaling kill clause appears new.
full_record.minimal_falsification_experiment: Train implicit and deconv heads of matched FLOPs on frozen features, evaluate mIoU/boundary-F at 1x and 2x resolution on ADE20K and Cityscapes, and verify the alias mechanism via frequency-domain analysis of error maps.
full_record.main_risk: Point-sampled training may converge slower, and compute matching by FLOPs may not match wall-clock or memory, muddying the fairness of the comparison.
full_record.community_default_belief: [MODEL SPECULATION] Boundary softness is attributed to coarse features, with the readout stack assumed to be a neutral resampler.
full_record.why_it_might_be_wrong: PointRend-style refinement may already capture most of this benefit, leaving the implicit head a marginal variant rather than a distinct capability.
full_record.fastest_falsification_experiment: Head-only trainings on frozen DINOv2 features for ADE20K take under 1 day total on one consumer GPU; datasets and backbones public.

one_line_idea: Anti-aliased patch embedding: replacing the ViT patchify stem with an anti-aliased convolutional downsampler measurably improves thin-structure segmentation at equal compute, because patchify aliases exactly the high-frequency content thin classes live in.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Thin-structure failure is partly stem-level information loss: sub-patch-width structures alias into unrecoverable feature noise at patchify, so an anti-aliased stem (low-pass filtered strided convolutions) preserves their evidence and improves thin-class IoU specifically, with negligible effect on thick classes.

full_record.one_line_idea: Anti-aliased patch embedding: replacing the ViT patchify stem with an anti-aliased convolutional downsampler measurably improves thin-structure segmentation at equal compute, because patchify aliases exactly the high-frequency content thin classes live in.
full_record.problem: [KNOWN FACT] ViT stems downsample by non-overlapping patch projection, a maximally aliasing operation, and dense predictors built on ViTs are notoriously weak on thin structures like poles and sign posts.
full_record.core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Thin-structure failure is partly stem-level information loss: sub-patch-width structures alias into unrecoverable feature noise at patchify, so an anti-aliased stem (low-pass filtered strided convolutions) preserves their evidence and improves thin-class IoU specifically, with negligible effect on thick classes.
full_record.falsifiable_prediction: [EXPECTED RESULT] Training matched ViT-S segmentation models on Cityscapes from identical initialization recipes, the anti-aliased stem will improve thin-class IoU (pole, traffic light, traffic sign) by at least 2.0 points with under 0.5 change on thick classes and under 3% compute overhead; kill the idea if thin-class gains are under 0.7 points, meaning the bottleneck lies deeper than the stem.
full_record.why_important: Identifies and repairs a concrete architectural aliasing mechanism behind a well-known failure mode, with a class-stratified prediction that cleanly separates the mechanism from generic capacity effects.
full_record.why_possibly_novel: [MODEL SPECULATION / unverified] Anti-aliased CNN downsampling is established; targeting the ViT patchify stem with a thin-class-stratified kill test appears unexamined.
full_record.minimal_falsification_experiment: Train ViT-S + UPerNet variants (patchify vs anti-aliased stem) on Cityscapes and ADE20K from scratch-equivalent schedules, report class-stratified IoU, and verify the mechanism by measuring stem-output energy for band-limited thin-structure probes.
full_record.main_risk: Stem changes alter optimization dynamics beyond aliasing (effective receptive fields, early-layer statistics), confounding the mechanism attribution despite matched budgets.
full_record.community_default_belief: [MODEL SPECULATION] Thin-structure weakness is attributed to token resolution and decoder design, with the stem treated as a neutral tokenizer.
full_record.why_it_might_be_wrong: Pretraining dominates dense quality; a stem fix evaluated without large-scale pretraining may show effects that vanish once models are pretrained at scale.

full_record.problem: [KNOWN FACT] Large ViTs develop high-norm artifact tokens that corrupt feature maps for dense use, and the register-token remedy is applied at pretraining time, leaving deployed checkpoints unrepaired.

full_record.falsifiable_prediction: [EXPECTED RESULT] Retrofitting registers into a public artifact-bearing ViT with a 20-epoch continued-pretraining phase on ImageNet-scale public data will remove at least 80% of high-norm outlier tokens and improve frozen-feature linear-probe mIoU on ADE20K by at least 1.5 points; kill the idea if outlier reduction is under 30% or dense-probe gains are under 0.5, meaning artifacts require from-scratch pretraining to fix.
full_record.why_important: Converts a pretraining-time insight into a retrofit capability applicable to the deployed checkpoint zoo, multiplying the reach of the register mechanism.
full_record.why_possibly_novel: [MODEL SPECULATION / unverified] Register tokens are established as a pretraining fix (ViT-registers lineage); the cheap-retrofit protocol with quantified artifact and probe outcomes appears untested.
full_record.minimal_falsification_experiment: Take a public artifact-bearing checkpoint, add 4 registers, continue pretraining briefly on ImageNet-1k with the original objective, and measure outlier-token statistics plus dense-probe deltas against the untouched checkpoint and a no-register continued-pretraining control.
full_record.main_risk: Continued pretraining itself (regardless of registers) may alter dense-probe scores, which the no-register control must cleanly separate.
full_record.community_default_belief: [MODEL SPECULATION] Artifact tokens are assumed baked in by pretraining and fixable only by re-pretraining with registers from scratch.
full_record.why_it_might_be_wrong: The global-statistics routing may be structurally entrenched in attention patterns that short continued training cannot re-route.
full_record.fastest_falsification_experiment: A 20-epoch continued pretraining of ViT-B on ImageNet-1k takes about 2-3 days on one A100 with modern recipes; ImageNet, ADE20K, and public checkpoints (timm/DINOv2 lineage) suffice.

one_line_idea: Resolution-extrapolation recipes for dense inference: a position-encoding rescaling law plus attention-temperature correction lets models trained at 512px infer at 2048px with minimal degradation, unlocking high-resolution deployment without high-resolution training.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Most extrapolation degradation in ViT-based dense models comes from two quantifiable shifts — position-encoding interpolation distortion and attention-entropy growth with token count — both of which admit closed-form corrections (log-linear PE rescaling; temperature scaled by log token count), so corrected models extrapolate gracefully without finetuning.

full_record.one_line_idea: Resolution-extrapolation recipes for dense inference: a position-encoding rescaling law plus attention-temperature correction lets models trained at 512px infer at 2048px with minimal degradation, unlocking high-resolution deployment without high-resolution training.
full_record.problem: [KNOWN FACT] Dense models degrade when inferring far above training resolution, and the standard remedies (multi-crop tiling or high-resolution finetuning) cost either context integrity or significant compute.
full_record.core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Most extrapolation degradation in ViT-based dense models comes from two quantifiable shifts — position-encoding interpolation distortion and attention-entropy growth with token count — both of which admit closed-form corrections (log-linear PE rescaling; temperature scaled by log token count), so corrected models extrapolate gracefully without finetuning.
full_record.falsifiable_prediction: [EXPECTED RESULT] On Cityscapes with a SegFormer/ViT model trained at 512px, corrected whole-image 2048px inference will retain at least 95% of native-resolution mIoU, versus at most 88% for naive extrapolation, and each correction will contribute measurably in ablation (at least 2 mIoU together); kill the idea if naive extrapolation already retains over 93% (nothing to fix) or corrections add under 1.0 mIoU (wrong mechanism).
full_record.why_important: High-resolution inference without tiling preserves global context for large scenes, and a training-free recipe is immediately adoptable by anyone deploying frozen dense models.
full_record.why_possibly_novel: [MODEL SPECULATION / unverified] PE interpolation and attention-entropy corrections circulate in language-model context extension; a validated dense-vision extrapolation recipe with mechanism-level ablations appears missing.
full_record.minimal_falsification_experiment: Evaluate whole-image inference at 1x/2x/4x training resolution with each correction toggled, on Cityscapes and ADE20K, and correlate degradation with measured attention-entropy shift per layer.
full_record.main_risk: Convolutional components (in hybrid heads) have their own resolution pathologies that these token-level corrections do not address, capping retention regardless.
full_record.community_default_belief: [MODEL SPECULATION] Resolution extrapolation is assumed to require finetuning or tiling, and inference resolution is pinned to training resolution as a rule of practice.
full_record.why_it_might_be_wrong: Degradation may be dominated by scale mismatch between object sizes seen at training and test, a data-statistics issue no encoding correction can fix.
full_record.fastest_falsification_experiment: Inference-only sweeps with public MMSegmentation checkpoints on Cityscapes and ADE20K run in under 6 hours on one consumer GPU; all public.

one_line_idea: Annotation-convention directions in weight space: interpolating between checkpoints finetuned on two mask conventions traces a monotone boundary-style continuum, giving deployment-time convention control from a single stored direction vector.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Because convention differences are a systematic low-complexity output transformation, the weight-space displacement between same-base checkpoints finetuned under two conventions acts as a convention direction: interpolation coefficients map monotonically onto boundary-style statistics, making the direction a control knob rather than a lottery.

full_record.one_line_idea: Annotation-convention directions in weight space: interpolating between checkpoints finetuned on two mask conventions traces a monotone boundary-style continuum, giving deployment-time convention control from a single stored direction vector.
full_record.problem: [KNOWN FACT] Models must commit to one annotation convention at training time, and serving users with different convention needs requires separate checkpoints.
full_record.core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Because convention differences are a systematic low-complexity output transformation, the weight-space displacement between same-base checkpoints finetuned under two conventions acts as a convention direction: interpolation coefficients map monotonically onto boundary-style statistics, making the direction a control knob rather than a lottery.
full_record.falsifiable_prediction: [EXPECTED RESULT] Interpolating between COCO-convention and LVIS-convention finetunes of one base Mask2Former, boundary-tightness statistics of the outputs will vary monotonically with the coefficient (Spearman rho at least 0.9 across 11 steps), and the midpoint model will score within 1.5 mask-AP of convention-specific models when evaluated under a synthetic mid-convention reference; kill the idea if interpolation is non-monotone or midpoint quality collapses by over 5 AP (loss barrier), meaning conventions are not linearly connected.
full_record.why_important: One stored direction replacing per-convention checkpoints is a practical serving capability and evidence that label conventions occupy structured weight-space directions, a reusable scientific finding.
full_record.why_possibly_novel: [MODEL SPECULATION / unverified] Weight interpolation between finetunes is studied for accuracy-robustness tradeoffs; convention control as the interpolation axis with a monotonicity kill test appears new.
full_record.minimal_falsification_experiment: Finetune one base under each convention on the dual-annotated COCO/LVIS overlap, sweep interpolation, and measure boundary-tightness monotonicity plus AP under both conventions at each step.
full_record.main_risk: The two finetunes may drift apart in unrelated directions (data order, augmentation), burying the convention signal inside a noisy displacement vector.
full_record.community_default_belief: [MODEL SPECULATION] Weight interpolation between differently supervised models is expected to produce loss barriers, not controllable intermediate behavior.
full_record.why_it_might_be_wrong: Convention differences may be too category-idiosyncratic for one global direction to express, showing monotonicity on average but incoherence per class.
full_record.fastest_falsification_experiment: Two Mask2Former finetunes on the public COCO/LVIS dual-annotation overlap plus interpolation sweeps run in about 1.5 days on one A100; all public.

one_line_idea: Procrustes head transplants: aligning feature spaces with an orthogonal map fitted on unlabeled images lets a task head trained on an old backbone run on a new backbone, recovering most performance with zero task-label retraining.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Dense feature spaces of successive backbone generations are related by an approximately orthogonal transformation identifiable from unlabeled data alone (matching feature statistics on shared images), so head transplantation via Procrustes alignment recovers most task performance, with the residual gap measuring genuinely new information in the upgraded backbone.

full_record.problem: [KNOWN FACT] Backbone upgrades orphan every trained task head, and retraining heads requires task labels and compute that many deployments no longer have access to.
full_record.core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Dense feature spaces of successive backbone generations are related by an approximately orthogonal transformation identifiable from unlabeled data alone (matching feature statistics on shared images), so head transplantation via Procrustes alignment recovers most task performance, with the residual gap measuring genuinely new information in the upgraded backbone.
full_record.falsifiable_prediction: [EXPECTED RESULT] Transplanting a detection head trained on DINOv2 ViT-B features onto DINOv2 ViT-L (and onto OpenCLIP ViT-B) via orthogonal alignment fitted on 5k unlabeled COCO images will recover at least 70% of the box AP that full head retraining on the new backbone achieves; kill the idea if recovery is under 40% for the within-family transplant, meaning even sibling feature spaces are not orthogonally alignable at dense granularity.
full_record.why_important: Zero-label backbone upgrades are a deployment capability with immediate value wherever labels are private, expired, or expensive, and the recovery fraction is a clean measure of representational continuity across model generations.
full_record.why_possibly_novel: [MODEL SPECULATION / unverified] Model stitching uses trained adapters with labels; label-free orthogonal transplantation for dense heads with a recovery benchmark appears new.
full_record.minimal_falsification_experiment: Fit orthogonal maps between backbone pairs on unlabeled images, transplant frozen detection/segmentation heads, and compare against label-based head retraining and no-alignment controls on COCO and ADE20K.
full_record.main_risk: Orthogonality is a strong constraint; if the true relation involves scaling and subspace reweighting, recovery may hinge on relaxations that require labels to fit, undermining the zero-label story.
full_record.community_default_belief: [MODEL SPECULATION] Head retraining after backbone changes is treated as unavoidable, with feature spaces assumed incompatibly reorganized across generations.
full_record.why_it_might_be_wrong: Detection heads consume multi-scale features whose cross-backbone correspondence may be layer-permuted, breaking any single-layer alignment scheme.
full_record.fastest_falsification_experiment: Alignment fitting (hours, unlabeled) plus inference evaluations and one reference Faster R-CNN head retraining (DINOv2 backbones) on COCO subsets take about 2 days on one A100; all checkpoints and data public.

one_line_idea: Dense-task finetuning edits are layer-sparse: most of a task vector's effect concentrates in a small fraction of layers, so sparse task-delta storage and merging preserve capability at a fifth of the memory and interference cost.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Dense-task adaptation is functionally localized: a small subset of layers (late blocks and decoder interfaces) carries nearly all task-relevant change, so truncating task vectors to their top-energy layers preserves single-task performance and reduces multi-task merge interference because deltas overlap less.

full_record.one_line_idea: Dense-task finetuning edits are layer-sparse: most of a task vector's effect concentrates in a small fraction of layers, so sparse task-delta storage and merging preserve capability at a fifth of the memory and interference cost.
full_record.problem: [KNOWN FACT] Task vectors are stored and merged as full-model deltas, and merging many tasks accumulates interference across all layers simultaneously.
full_record.core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Dense-task adaptation is functionally localized: a small subset of layers (late blocks and decoder interfaces) carries nearly all task-relevant change, so truncating task vectors to their top-energy layers preserves single-task performance and reduces multi-task merge interference because deltas overlap less.
full_record.falsifiable_prediction: [EXPECTED RESULT] For detection and segmentation finetunes of a shared ViT base, task vectors truncated to the top 20% of layers by delta energy will retain at least 95% of full-delta task performance, and three-task merges of truncated vectors will beat full-vector merges by at least 1.5 points average; kill the idea if truncation to 20% of layers loses over 15% of single-task performance, meaning dense adaptation is functionally distributed.
full_record.why_important: Establishes a locality law for dense-task adaptation that directly enables cheaper checkpoint logistics and better merging, tying a scientific claim to an operational payoff.
full_record.why_possibly_novel: [MODEL SPECULATION / unverified] Delta sparsification appears in NLP merging work; a layer-level locality characterization for dense perception tasks with merge-interference consequences appears new.
full_record.minimal_falsification_experiment: Compute per-layer delta energies for public dense finetunes, evaluate truncated-delta models across energy thresholds, and run three-task merges (detection, semantic, keypoints) under full vs truncated deltas.
full_record.main_risk: Delta energy may mislocate functional importance (small deltas in sensitive layers matter more), requiring causal layer-patching controls that complicate the story.
full_record.community_default_belief: [MODEL SPECULATION] Finetuning is assumed to spread task information diffusely across all layers, making full deltas the safe default.
full_record.why_it_might_be_wrong: Layer sparsity may hold for heads-adjacent layers trivially while the claimed backbone locality fails, reducing the finding to the obvious.
full_record.fastest_falsification_experiment: Using public finetuned checkpoints (MMDetection/MMSegmentation ViT-based) plus truncation and merge evaluations on COCO/ADE20K subsets takes about 1 day on one GPU; all public.

one_line_idea: Pre-merge orthogonalization: projecting task vectors to reduce their pairwise conflict before merging recovers a large share of the performance lost to interference, turning merge quality from a lottery into a controlled procedure.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Merge degradation is dominated by conflicting components of task vectors in a low-dimensional shared subspace; orthogonalizing task vectors against each other's high-curvature directions (estimated from cheap Fisher approximations) before averaging removes the destructive interference while keeping each task's private components, recovering most of the specialist gap.

full_record.one_line_idea: Pre-merge orthogonalization: projecting task vectors to reduce their pairwise conflict before merging recovers a large share of the performance lost to interference, turning merge quality from a lottery into a controlled procedure.
full_record.problem: [KNOWN FACT] Multi-task weight merging loses performance as tasks are added, and existing remedies (sign election, magnitude pruning) treat symptoms without an explicit interference model.
full_record.core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Merge degradation is dominated by conflicting components of task vectors in a low-dimensional shared subspace; orthogonalizing task vectors against each other's high-curvature directions (estimated from cheap Fisher approximations) before averaging removes the destructive interference while keeping each task's private components, recovering most of the specialist gap.
full_record.falsifiable_prediction: [EXPECTED RESULT] Merging three dense-task specialists (semantic segmentation, detection, human keypoints) from a shared ViT base, Fisher-guided orthogonalization will recover at least 50% of the average per-task gap between naive task-arithmetic merging and individual specialists, and beat TIES-style sign election by at least 1.0 point average; kill the idea if recovery over naive merging is under 20%, meaning interference is not subspace-structured.
full_record.why_important: A working interference model upgrades merging from heuristic to engineering discipline, enabling one-checkpoint deployment of perception suites on edge systems.
full_record.why_possibly_novel: [MODEL SPECULATION / unverified] Sign-election and pruning heuristics exist (TIES lineage); explicit curvature-guided orthogonalization for dense perception merges with a recovery-fraction kill line appears new.
full_record.minimal_falsification_experiment: Finetune three specialists from one base, estimate diagonal/low-rank Fisher per task on 1k images each, orthogonalize and merge under several projection strengths, and compare per-task metrics against naive, TIES, and specialist references.
full_record.main_risk: Cheap Fisher approximations may misidentify the conflict subspace, and the projection could remove task-critical components exactly for the most distinctive task.
full_record.community_default_belief: [MODEL SPECULATION] Merge interference is treated as an unavoidable tax, with per-task adapters seen as the only reliable multi-task deployment path.
full_record.why_it_might_be_wrong: Interference may be intrinsically high-rank for dense tasks, in which case no projection preserves all tasks and adapters remain strictly better.
full_record.fastest_falsification_experiment: Three specialist finetunes (ViT-B UPerNet / Faster R-CNN / ViTPose-style head) on COCO/ADE20K subsets plus merge sweeps run in about 4 days on one A100; all models and data public.

one_line_idea: Vocabulary-union merging: two detectors finetuned from one base on disjoint category sets merge into a single model detecting the union within a small gap of joint training, eliminating the need to pool datasets for vocabulary growth.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Category knowledge added by finetuning is largely additive in weight space when categories are disjoint (their classifier and mask/box heads occupy separate output slots and their backbone deltas are small and compatible), so merging two disjoint-vocabulary finetunes approximates joint training, with degradation concentrated in categories that are visually confusable across the two sets.

full_record.one_line_idea: Vocabulary-union merging: two detectors finetuned from one base on disjoint category sets merge into a single model detecting the union within a small gap of joint training, eliminating the need to pool datasets for vocabulary growth.
full_record.problem: [KNOWN FACT] Extending a detector's vocabulary currently requires joint training on combined datasets, which is blocked when datasets cannot be co-located or re-trained at will.
full_record.core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Category knowledge added by finetuning is largely additive in weight space when categories are disjoint (their classifier and mask/box heads occupy separate output slots and their backbone deltas are small and compatible), so merging two disjoint-vocabulary finetunes approximates joint training, with degradation concentrated in categories that are visually confusable across the two sets.
full_record.falsifiable_prediction: [EXPECTED RESULT] Splitting COCO's 80 classes into two disjoint 40-class finetunes from a shared base and merging, union-evaluation AP will come within 3.0 points of the jointly trained reference, and per-class degradation will correlate with cross-set visual confusability (feature-space class distance) at Spearman rho at least 0.5; kill the idea if the union gap exceeds 8 AP, meaning vocabulary knowledge is not weight-additive.
full_record.why_important: Merge-based vocabulary growth is a deployment capability for federated and licensing-constrained settings, and the confusability correlation gives it a predictive theory of when it fails.
full_record.why_possibly_novel: [MODEL SPECULATION / unverified] Open-vocabulary and incremental detection exist as training paradigms; weight-space vocabulary union with a confusability-based failure model appears new.
full_record.minimal_falsification_experiment: Create the disjoint splits, finetune both halves from one Faster R-CNN base, merge with task arithmetic plus output-slot concatenation, and evaluate union AP against joint training with the confusability regression.
full_record.main_risk: Background-class semantics differ between the halves (each treats the other's categories as background), injecting a systematic conflict the merge cannot resolve without a data pass.
full_record.community_default_belief: [MODEL SPECULATION] Vocabulary extension is assumed to require data-level joint training or distillation, not weight-level composition.
full_record.why_it_might_be_wrong: The background-conflict mechanism may dominate everything, making merged models hallucinate or suppress across sets and burying the additive structure.
full_record.fastest_falsification_experiment: Three Faster R-CNN trainings on COCO 40-class splits (MMDetection, 1x) plus merges take about 3 single-A100 days; COCO and base checkpoints public.

one_line_idea: Interaction-noise training for prompt robustness: injecting realistic misclick and imprecision noise into prompt simulation during training halves output variance under real-user-level prompt jitter without degrading clean-prompt accuracy.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Prompt sensitivity is an artifact of the clean-prompt training distribution rather than an inherent property: training with an empirically calibrated interaction-noise model (spatial jitter, wrong-instance clicks at plausible rates) smooths the prompt-to-output map, reducing jitter variance at no cost to clean performance because the noise model covers rather than replaces the clean cases.

full_record.core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Box-drawing slack is a supervision noise floor for localization: replacing drawn boxes with mask-tight refits where masks exist removes a biased noise component, so models trained on refit boxes improve specifically at strict IoU thresholds (AP75, AP90) where slack dominates the error budget.
full_record.falsifiable_prediction: [EXPECTED RESULT] Training public detectors on COCO with mask-refit boxes will improve AP75 by at least 1.0 and AP90 by at least 1.5 points at AP50 within 0.3 of baseline, and the improvement will scale with each class's measured drawn-box slack (rho at least 0.5); kill the idea if AP75 gains are under 0.3, meaning drawn-box noise is below the learning noise floor.
full_record.why_important: A free supervision upgrade for every masked detection dataset, plus a quantified accounting of how much localization ceiling is annotation slack rather than model limitation.
full_record.why_possibly_novel: [MODEL SPECULATION / unverified] Mask-to-box conversion is trivial tooling; treating drawn-box slack as a measurable supervision noise source with strict-threshold predictions appears unexamined.
full_record.minimal_falsification_experiment: Measure drawn-vs-refit box deltas on COCO, retrain Faster R-CNN and DINO-DETR on refit boxes, evaluate the AP threshold spectrum, and run the per-class slack-to-gain regression.
full_record.main_risk: Evaluation ground truth keeps drawn-box conventions, so refit-trained models could be penalized at test time for being right, requiring dual evaluation against refit and original references.
full_record.community_default_belief: [MODEL SPECULATION] Ground-truth boxes are treated as definitionally correct targets, with localization improvements sought entirely on the model side.
full_record.why_it_might_be_wrong: Mask boundary errors may inject as much noise as box slack removes, netting zero at every threshold.
full_record.fastest_falsification_experiment: Box refitting is scripted; two detector retrainings on COCO (MMDetection 1x) take about 2 single-A100 days; all public.

full_record.why_important: Unlocks part supervision at keypoint-archive scale for human-centric perception, with the dilation control separating the propagation mechanism from the mere existence of skeletal supervision.
full_record.why_possibly_novel: [MODEL SPECULATION / unverified] Pose-guided parsing exists with joint training; a pure bootstrap from keypoints to competitive part segmentation with a mechanism control appears untested.
full_record.minimal_falsification_experiment: Generate pseudo-masks from COCO keypoints via geodesic propagation on DINOv2 features, train a SegFormer part model, and evaluate against fully supervised LIP training and the dilation-control variant.
full_record.main_risk: Loose clothing decouples part extents from bone geometry, and the propagation may systematically fail on exactly the clothing-heavy imagery where part parsing is most used.

full_record.why_it_might_be_wrong: Feature geodesics may leak across adjacent limbs in contact poses, corrupting pseudo-masks precisely where parsing is hard and capping the recoverable fraction.

one_line_idea: Underwater detectors implicitly regress object range from wavelength-dependent color loss, so swapping the water's optical type at test time moves detections in a direction predictable from attenuation physics.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Detection confidence in underwater models is partly a function of the red-to-blue channel ratio acting as a learned range prior, so physically re-rendering the same scene under a different Jerlov-style water type will shift confidences in the direction predicted by the attenuation coefficients, not randomly.

full_record.one_line_idea: Underwater detectors implicitly regress object range from wavelength-dependent color loss, so swapping the water's optical type at test time moves detections in a direction predictable from attenuation physics.
full_record.problem: [KNOWN FACT] Water absorbs red light far faster than blue-green, so an object's color balance shifts systematically with camera-to-object distance; underwater detection models are trained and evaluated without controlling for this coupling.
full_record.core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Detection confidence in underwater models is partly a function of the red-to-blue channel ratio acting as a learned range prior, so physically re-rendering the same scene under a different Jerlov-style water type will shift confidences in the direction predicted by the attenuation coefficients, not randomly.
full_record.falsifiable_prediction: [EXPECTED RESULT] Re-attenuating test images from coastal-type to oceanic-type water (physically parameterized channel-wise exponential re-rendering with known per-channel coefficients) will change per-object confidence with a sign agreement of at least 70% with the physics-predicted direction; kill the idea if sign agreement is below 55% (chance-like) or if confidence shifts are uncorrelated with the applied per-channel attenuation delta (|r| < 0.2).
full_record.why_important: If color-as-range is load-bearing, cross-site underwater deployment failures are predictable and correctable from water optical properties measured with a $100 transmissometer reading rather than requiring new labels.
full_record.why_possibly_novel: [MODEL SPECULATION / unverified] Underwater enhancement work manipulates color for human viewing, but a signed, physics-predicted confidence-shift test on detectors appears untested.
full_record.minimal_falsification_experiment: Take a public underwater detection set, estimate per-image channel attenuation, re-render each image under two other water types via channel-wise exponential scaling with plausible ranges, run a trained detector, and test sign agreement between confidence deltas and physics-predicted deltas.
full_record.main_risk: Per-image attenuation estimation without known range maps is noisy, which could dilute the signed prediction even if the mechanism is real.
full_record.community_default_belief: [MODEL SPECULATION] Practitioners treat underwater color shift as generic domain gap to be erased by enhancement or augmentation, not as a structured range cue the model has internalized.
full_record.why_it_might_be_wrong: Detectors may rely mostly on shape and local contrast, with color contributing too little for a measurable signed shift.
full_record.fastest_falsification_experiment: Public data and model: DUO or RUOD underwater detection images with a YOLOv8 checkpoint fine-tuned on the same training split; channel-wise re-rendering plus inference over 2k images is under 6 GPU-hours on one consumer GPU (~$10).

full_record.falsifiable_prediction: [EXPECTED RESULT] Recall for objects in the darkest image quartile will be at least 25 points lower than in the brightest quartile at matched object size, and illumination flattening will recover at least a third of that deficit; kill the idea if the dark-quartile deficit is under 8 points or flattening recovers under 10% of it.
full_record.why_important: Ecological surveys quantify abundance from ROV video; an irradiance-conditional recall function biases abundance estimates toward the light cone and is correctable in software once characterized.
full_record.why_possibly_novel: [MODEL SPECULATION / unverified] Deep-sea ML papers report overall mAP; an irradiance-stratified recall law with a flattening intervention appears unmeasured.

full_record.main_risk: Irradiance correlates with substrate type and altitude, so stratification needs care to avoid attributing habitat effects to lighting.

full_record.why_possibly_novel: [MODEL SPECULATION / unverified] Refractive geometry is standard in underwater photogrammetry, but nobody appears to have tested whether foundation depth models inherit the predicted radial bias or whether physical pre-warping fixes them zero-shot.

full_record.main_risk: Some datasets use dome ports (which approximately restore single-viewpoint geometry), which would dilute the effect if port metadata is missing.

one_line_idea: Scanner-to-scanner color shift in pathology is a low-dimensional physical transform (illuminant plus sensor response), estimable from unlabeled tiles without correspondence, and applying the estimated transform recovers most cross-scanner accuracy without retraining.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Because the physical chain is approximately a per-channel linear map in optical-density space, the scanner shift is captured by a low-parameter transform (under 12 parameters) that can be estimated by matching stain-vector statistics between unlabeled tile populations, and applying it at inference recovers the majority of the cross-scanner drop for a frozen model.

full_record.problem: [KNOWN FACT] The same glass slide scanned on two devices yields different colors due to illuminant spectra, filters, and sensor response; deployed models degrade on unseen scanners and current fixes retrain or heavily augment.

full_record.why_important: A correspondence-free 12-parameter calibration is deployable in clinical IT within existing validation frameworks, unlike retraining; it also cleanly measures how much of 'scanner shift' is color at all.
full_record.why_possibly_novel: [MODEL SPECULATION / unverified] Stain normalization is a crowded field; framing scanner shift as an identifiable low-parameter physical transform with a recovery-fraction kill test against non-color residuals appears sharper than existing comparisons.

one_line_idea: OCR and handwriting models increasingly read from language priors instead of pixels as degradation grows, measurable by a matched pseudoword substitution test whose accuracy gap quantifies hallucination risk.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] The visual-evidence share of recognition can be isolated by comparing accuracy on real words versus orthographically matched pseudowords rendered/written identically: the word-pseudoword gap grows monotonically with degradation strength and differs sharply across architectures, providing a scalar 'prior dominance index' that predicts hallucinated-content rates on named entities.

full_record.one_line_idea: OCR and handwriting models increasingly read from language priors instead of pixels as degradation grows, measurable by a matched pseudoword substitution test whose accuracy gap quantifies hallucination risk.
full_record.problem: [KNOWN FACT] Modern text recognizers embed strong implicit language models; under degradation they output plausible words, and errors are increasingly 'fluent' substitutions rather than character garbles, which is dangerous for names, numbers, and codes.
full_record.core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] The visual-evidence share of recognition can be isolated by comparing accuracy on real words versus orthographically matched pseudowords rendered/written identically: the word-pseudoword gap grows monotonically with degradation strength and differs sharply across architectures, providing a scalar 'prior dominance index' that predicts hallucinated-content rates on named entities.
full_record.falsifiable_prediction: [EXPECTED RESULT] The word-vs-pseudoword accuracy gap will at least triple from clean to heavily degraded conditions, and models ranked by this index will rank identically (Spearman rho >= 0.7) on named-entity hallucination rates in a held-out corpus; kill the idea if the gap stays flat with degradation or the index fails to predict entity hallucination (rho < 0.3).
full_record.why_important: Archives, banking, and legal pipelines need to know when an OCR output is evidence versus guesswork; a portable index of prior dominance directly supports deployment policy (e.g., route high-index conditions to human review).
full_record.why_possibly_novel: [MODEL SPECULATION / unverified] Psycholinguistics uses pseudowords routinely; using matched pseudoword rendering as an instrument to decompose OCR into visual versus prior components appears untested.
full_record.minimal_falsification_experiment: Generate matched word/pseudoword pairs, render or collect them in identical visual conditions, sweep degradation strength, and measure the accuracy gap per model; validate the index against entity-level hallucination on real degraded documents.
full_record.main_risk: Pseudoword handwriting samples are scarce; synthetic rendering covers print OCR well but handwriting requires style-transfer generation with its own artifacts.
full_record.community_default_belief: [MODEL SPECULATION] Language priors in OCR are viewed as purely beneficial; hallucination is treated anecdotally rather than as a measurable, growing function of degradation.
full_record.why_it_might_be_wrong: Character-level decoders may show negligible word/pseudoword gaps even degraded, making the index trivial for half the model zoo.
full_record.fastest_falsification_experiment: Public data and model: IAM handwriting and rendered corpora with TrOCR and Tesseract; the full sweep runs in about 8 GPU-hours on one consumer GPU (~$15).

one_line_idea: Bleed-through in double-sided historical documents is a mirrored, blurred copy of the verso page, so jointly modeling recto and verso scans inverts it physically and beats single-side restoration for downstream recognition.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Because the interference source is available (the verso scan predicts the bleed-through pattern up to a mirror transform, per-region attenuation, and a diffusion kernel), a two-input model that explicitly registers and subtracts the transformed verso will remove bleed-through more accurately than any single-image method, with the largest gains where recto and verso strokes overlap.

full_record.one_line_idea: Bleed-through in double-sided historical documents is a mirrored, blurred copy of the verso page, so jointly modeling recto and verso scans inverts it physically and beats single-side restoration for downstream recognition.
full_record.problem: [KNOWN FACT] Ink from the reverse side shows through aged paper as a mirrored, attenuated, slightly diffused image; archives usually scan both sides, yet restoration methods treat each side independently as generic noise removal.
full_record.core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Because the interference source is available (the verso scan predicts the bleed-through pattern up to a mirror transform, per-region attenuation, and a diffusion kernel), a two-input model that explicitly registers and subtracts the transformed verso will remove bleed-through more accurately than any single-image method, with the largest gains where recto and verso strokes overlap.
full_record.falsifiable_prediction: [EXPECTED RESULT] Joint recto-verso restoration will cut downstream character error rate on bleed-through-affected regions by at least 30% relative to the best single-side baseline, with gains concentrated (at least 2x) in stroke-overlap regions; kill the idea if the relative CER gain is under 10%.
full_record.why_important: Millions of archival pages suffer bleed-through; the verso scan is an unused, freely available side channel that turns an ill-posed inpainting problem into a well-posed source-separation problem.
full_record.why_possibly_novel: [MODEL SPECULATION / unverified] Classical recto-verso separation was studied pre-deep-learning on small examples; integrating it with learned registration and evaluating by downstream recognition on public benchmarks appears open.
full_record.minimal_falsification_experiment: Pair recto/verso scans from public archival collections, train the two-input restoration model against single-side baselines, and evaluate OCR/HTR error on affected regions.
full_record.main_risk: Non-rigid paper distortion between the two scans complicates registration; failure of registration silently degrades to the single-side baseline.
full_record.community_default_belief: [MODEL SPECULATION] Bleed-through is bundled into generic document enhancement, and the verso side is ignored as a modeling input.
full_record.why_it_might_be_wrong: Heavy diffusion through thick paper may destroy the geometric correspondence needed for subtraction to beat learned single-side priors.
full_record.fastest_falsification_experiment: Public data and model: DIBCO document binarization benchmarks (bleed-through examples) plus double-sided pages from public archives, with Tesseract/TrOCR as downstream readers; the pilot runs in about 10 GPU-hours on one consumer GPU (~$20).

one_line_idea: Binarization, still the first step of many document pipelines, destroys stroke-interior and grayscale evidence that end-to-end recognizers exploit, and the information loss can be quantified as a degradation-dependent CER penalty law.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] The recognition penalty from binarization grows with degradation (faint ink, stains) because grayscale carries the discriminative evidence there, so the penalty curve (CER with binarization minus CER without, as a function of degradation level) rises steeply, and binarization quality metrics fail to predict the penalty across binarization algorithms.

full_record.one_line_idea: Binarization, still the first step of many document pipelines, destroys stroke-interior and grayscale evidence that end-to-end recognizers exploit, and the information loss can be quantified as a degradation-dependent CER penalty law.
full_record.problem: [KNOWN FACT] Historical document pipelines inherited a binarize-then-recognize structure from the fax era; competitions still optimize binarization quality metrics as if they were proxies for recognition quality.
full_record.core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] The recognition penalty from binarization grows with degradation (faint ink, stains) because grayscale carries the discriminative evidence there, so the penalty curve (CER with binarization minus CER without, as a function of degradation level) rises steeply, and binarization quality metrics fail to predict the penalty across binarization algorithms.
full_record.falsifiable_prediction: [EXPECTED RESULT] The binarization CER penalty will at least quadruple from clean to degraded strata, and rank correlation between binarization quality metrics and actual downstream CER across algorithms will be under 0.4; kill the idea if the penalty stays under 5% relative everywhere or if quality metrics predict CER at rho >= 0.7, which would validate the legacy pipeline.
full_record.why_important: The result would redirect a whole competition ecosystem: if binarization metrics do not predict recognition outcomes, the field is optimizing a proxy detached from its purpose.
full_record.why_possibly_novel: [MODEL SPECULATION / unverified] End-to-end superiority is folklore; a pre-registered penalty law across degradation strata plus the metric-decoupling test appears undone.
full_record.minimal_falsification_experiment: Run matched recognizers on grayscale versus binarized versions of public benchmarks stratified by degradation, sweeping several binarization algorithms, and correlate binarization metrics with downstream CER.
full_record.main_risk: Recognizers trained mostly on clean data may underuse grayscale evidence, understating the true information loss.
full_record.community_default_belief: [MODEL SPECULATION] Binarization is treated as harmless normalization, and its competition metrics as meaningful quality measures.
full_record.why_it_might_be_wrong: For extremely degraded pages, binarization might act as beneficial regularization that end-to-end models cannot replicate, inverting the penalty.
full_record.fastest_falsification_experiment: Public data and model: DIBCO strata plus IAM/GT4HistOCR with TrOCR and Tesseract; the sweep runs in about 6 GPU-hours on one consumer GPU (~$12).

one_line_idea: Reading order is the invisible output dimension of document AI: systems with identical detection scores can scramble token order enough to corrupt downstream LLM consumption, and an order-sensitive metric exposes large hidden quality differences.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Reading-order quality varies widely among systems whose detection/recognition metrics tie, and this variation causally affects downstream task performance: LLM question-answering over linearized documents degrades roughly linearly with normalized order inversions injected at controlled rates, so order metrics deserve first-class status.

full_record.one_line_idea: Reading order is the invisible output dimension of document AI: systems with identical detection scores can scramble token order enough to corrupt downstream LLM consumption, and an order-sensitive metric exposes large hidden quality differences.
full_record.problem: [KNOWN FACT] Document parsing feeds LLMs via linearized text; evaluation focuses on per-token or per-region accuracy, while the sequence in which regions are linearized (columns, insets, captions, footnotes) is scored loosely or not at all.
full_record.core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Reading-order quality varies widely among systems whose detection/recognition metrics tie, and this variation causally affects downstream task performance: LLM question-answering over linearized documents degrades roughly linearly with normalized order inversions injected at controlled rates, so order metrics deserve first-class status.
full_record.falsifiable_prediction: [EXPECTED RESULT] Across parsing systems matched within 1 point of detection F1, normalized Kendall-tau order scores will span at least 15 points, and injecting inversions at the observed rates into ground-truth text will reduce downstream QA accuracy by at least 5 points; kill the idea if order scores cluster within 5 points or QA is insensitive (<1 point) to observed inversion rates.
full_record.why_important: Retrieval-augmented and document-QA stacks silently inherit order errors; quantifying the causal chain from order to answer quality justifies (or kills) investment in order-aware document models.
full_record.why_possibly_novel: [MODEL SPECULATION / unverified] Reading-order datasets exist, but the causal injection experiment linking measured inversion rates to downstream LLM degradation appears absent.
full_record.minimal_falsification_experiment: Evaluate public parsing systems on reading-order-annotated documents, measure order metrics at matched detection quality, then inject matched inversion rates into clean text and measure downstream QA deltas.
full_record.main_risk: Downstream sensitivity depends on task type (extraction vs summarization), so conclusions must be stratified rather than averaged.
full_record.community_default_belief: [MODEL SPECULATION] Reading order is assumed nearly solved by top-to-bottom, left-to-right heuristics with layout awareness treated as polish.
full_record.why_it_might_be_wrong: Modern LLMs may be robust to local order scrambling, absorbing inversions without measurable answer degradation.
