one_line_idea: Table understanding fails structurally on merged and nested cells because decoders emit token sequences without grid-consistency constraints; grammar-constrained decoding eliminates a specific, countable class of structural errors.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] A measurable share of table-structure errors are grid-inconsistency errors (overlapping spans, non-tiling cells) that constrained decoding provably cannot emit, so enforcing grid consistency at decode time removes that share entirely while leaving content recognition unchanged, with gains concentrated on merged/nested-cell tables.

full_record.problem: [KNOWN FACT] Tables are 2D grammatical objects (row/column spans must tile the grid), yet dominant models decode HTML-like token streams that can be syntactically valid but geometrically impossible; structure metrics average over error types, hiding this class.

full_record.why_important: Financial and scientific data extraction depends on table structure; removing a whole error class by construction is more reliable than more training data, and the audit itself tells us where structure errors come from.
full_record.why_possibly_novel: [MODEL SPECULATION / unverified] Constrained decoding is standard in parsing; a quantified error-class decomposition for table models plus the targeted-elimination test appears unreported.

full_record.main_risk: Constraint enforcement can push errors around (the model emits a different wrong-but-legal structure), so the audit must track total error movement, not just the eliminated class.
full_record.community_default_belief: [MODEL SPECULATION] Table errors are attributed to visual ambiguity of rules and cell boundaries, not to unconstrained decoders.
full_record.why_it_might_be_wrong: Modern models may have implicitly learned grid legality, making impossible outputs rare already.

one_line_idea: A page is internally consistent in hand and typeface, so per-page unsupervised adaptation (estimating one style code per page and conditioning the decoder) should beat both global models and per-glyph adaptation on historical text.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Recognition error on hard typefaces is largely a style-mismatch problem, not a legibility problem: inferring a low-dimensional style code from a page's unlabeled glyph population and conditioning recognition on it recovers most of the rare-typeface deficit, because within-page glyph consistency makes the style identifiable without labels; this is a document-native structural prior (one page, one style), distinct from generic test-time adaptation which updates weights per sample without an identifiability argument.

full_record.one_line_idea: A page is internally consistent in hand and typeface, so per-page unsupervised adaptation (estimating one style code per page and conditioning the decoder) should beat both global models and per-glyph adaptation on historical text.
full_record.problem: [KNOWN FACT] Historical OCR error concentrates in rare typefaces and idiosyncratic hands; each page, however, is usually set in a single face or written by one hand, a strong structural prior that page-agnostic models ignore.
full_record.core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Recognition error on hard typefaces is largely a style-mismatch problem, not a legibility problem: inferring a low-dimensional style code from a page's unlabeled glyph population and conditioning recognition on it recovers most of the rare-typeface deficit, because within-page glyph consistency makes the style identifiable without labels; this is a document-native structural prior (one page, one style), distinct from generic test-time adaptation which updates weights per sample without an identifiability argument.
full_record.falsifiable_prediction: [EXPECTED RESULT] Page-level style conditioning will cut CER on rare-typeface pages by at least 25% relative while changing common-typeface CER by under 2% relative, and the gain will scale with page length (more glyphs, better style identification); kill the idea if rare-typeface gains are under 8% relative or show no page-length dependence, which would falsify the identifiability mechanism.
full_record.why_important: Digitization of pre-1900 print is bottlenecked by typeface diversity; a labels-free per-page mechanism with a testable identifiability signature would be adopted immediately by heritage OCR pipelines.
full_record.why_possibly_novel: [MODEL SPECULATION / unverified] Font adaptation and writer adaptation have long histories; the page-as-identifiable-style-unit framing with a page-length scaling falsification appears fresh.
full_record.minimal_falsification_experiment: Train a style-code encoder over page glyph populations on public historical corpora, condition a recognizer on it, and evaluate CER stratified by typeface rarity and page length against unconditioned and per-glyph-adapted baselines.
full_record.main_risk: Multi-face pages (emphasis, marginalia) violate the one-style assumption and need a mixture extension that weakens the clean story.
full_record.community_default_belief: [MODEL SPECULATION] Rare-typeface failure is treated as a data-coverage problem to be solved by synthetic font rendering at scale.
full_record.why_it_might_be_wrong: Rare typefaces may fail due to genuinely ambiguous glyph shapes (long-s, ligatures) that no style conditioning can resolve without language context.
full_record.fastest_falsification_experiment: Public data and model: GT4HistOCR with Calamari or TrOCR as the base recognizer; training and stratified evaluation run in about 15 GPU-hours on one consumer GPU (~$30).

one_line_idea: Repeated photocopying acts as an iterated contraction on glyph shapes with predictable attractors, so augmenting OCR training with physically iterated copy-degradation beats single-pass noise models for multi-generation documents.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] The copy operator is approximately a fixed nonlinear map whose iteration drives glyphs toward attractor shapes (loops fill, stems merge); OCR error therefore grows with copy generation in a predictable, accelerating way, and training with iterated-operator augmentation (not stronger single-pass noise) recovers a large share of the multi-generation deficit because it exposes the model to the attractor geometry.

full_record.one_line_idea: Repeated photocopying acts as an iterated contraction on glyph shapes with predictable attractors, so augmenting OCR training with physically iterated copy-degradation beats single-pass noise models for multi-generation documents.
full_record.problem: [KNOWN FACT] Archives and legal discovery are full of Nth-generation photocopies; each copy pass applies blur, thresholding, and gain nonlinearity, and the composition of many passes produces characteristic artifacts (filled counters, broken thin strokes) unlike any single-pass degradation.
full_record.core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] The copy operator is approximately a fixed nonlinear map whose iteration drives glyphs toward attractor shapes (loops fill, stems merge); OCR error therefore grows with copy generation in a predictable, accelerating way, and training with iterated-operator augmentation (not stronger single-pass noise) recovers a large share of the multi-generation deficit because it exposes the model to the attractor geometry.
full_record.falsifiable_prediction: [EXPECTED RESULT] CER will grow superlinearly with simulated copy generation, and iterated-operator augmentation will outperform intensity-matched single-pass augmentation by at least 15% relative CER on 4th-generation-plus documents; kill the idea if the two augmentations tie within 5% relative, meaning composition structure carries no information beyond degradation strength.
full_record.why_important: Multi-generation copies are a large, ignored slice of real-world OCR failure (legal, governmental, archival); the iterated-operator insight is cheap to implement and tests a general principle about compositional degradations.
full_record.why_possibly_novel: [MODEL SPECULATION / unverified] Document degradation models exist, but treating copy iteration as a dynamical system with attractors and testing composition-structure against strength-matched noise appears new.
full_record.minimal_falsification_experiment: Implement a calibrated copy operator (blur, nonlinearity, threshold, resample), verify its realism against genuine multi-generation copies, then train recognizers with iterated versus strength-matched single-pass augmentation and compare CER by generation.
full_record.main_risk: Calibrating the operator to real photocopier behavior needs a few genuine copy chains; miscalibration would blunt the comparison.
full_record.community_default_belief: [MODEL SPECULATION] Degradation is parameterized by strength, with composition assumed irrelevant once the marginal artifact statistics match.
full_record.why_it_might_be_wrong: Strength-matched single-pass noise with heavy-tailed parameters may already cover the attractor artifacts, nullifying the composition claim.
full_record.fastest_falsification_experiment: Public data and model: RVL-CDIP scans and IAM lines with TrOCR; operator implementation and the training comparison run in about 12 GPU-hours on one consumer GPU (~$25).

core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Explicitly detecting maximal whitespace separators and feeding them as tokens alongside ink regions provides the parser with the generative variable of layout, improving structure recovery most on dense multi-column and mixed layouts where ink-region adjacency is ambiguous.

full_record.problem: [KNOWN FACT] Layout models detect ink regions (text blocks, figures) and infer structure from their arrangement; typographers, by contrast, design documents around whitespace, which is the actual separator signal (column gutters, paragraph indents, section gaps).

full_record.main_risk: Scanned skew and noise corrupt whitespace detection precisely on the degraded pages where help is needed most.

one_line_idea: The born-digital-to-scan gap in document AI decomposes into measurable physical factors (geometric warp, sensor noise, illumination), and factor-wise ablation will show geometric warp dominates, redirecting augmentation effort.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] The drop is decomposable by applying physical factors one at a time to born-digital pages (parametric page warp, sensor noise models, illumination gradients) and measuring marginal damage; warp will account for the largest share for layout tasks because it breaks the axis-aligned geometry priors learned from PDFs, while noise dominates only for recognition tasks.

full_record.one_line_idea: The born-digital-to-scan gap in document AI decomposes into measurable physical factors (geometric warp, sensor noise, illumination), and factor-wise ablation will show geometric warp dominates, redirecting augmentation effort.

full_record.falsifiable_prediction: [EXPECTED RESULT] The three factors will explain at least 70% of the born-digital-to-scan layout-F1 drop, with warp alone at least 40% of it; kill the idea if the factors jointly explain under 40% (meaning the gap is driven by unmodeled content differences) or if the factor ranking flips across two independent scan test sets.
full_record.why_important: A validated decomposition converts augmentation design from folklore to allocation: teams spend effort proportional to measured factor shares, and corpus builders know what to add.
full_record.why_possibly_novel: [MODEL SPECULATION / unverified] Domain gap decompositions exist in other areas; a pre-registered physical-factor accounting for the document born-digital-to-scan gap appears missing.

full_record.main_risk: Factors interact (warp changes how illumination gradients land), so an additive attribution may need interaction terms to close the accounting.

full_record.why_it_might_be_wrong: Content differences (real scans are older documents with different layouts) may dominate, making the physical decomposition explain little.

one_line_idea: Cross-page structure (running headers, footers, continued articles) is trivially identifiable by inter-page matching yet routinely misparsed by single-page models; a cross-page voting layer eliminates a whole error class in book and report parsing.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] A large, countable share of layout-classification errors on long documents are furniture confusions (headers/footers classified as body text or titles), and because furniture repeats with near-identical geometry and content across pages, a simple cross-page matching-and-voting layer identifies it with near-perfect precision, removing that error class without retraining the page model.

full_record.why_possibly_novel: [MODEL SPECULATION / unverified] Header/footer heuristics are old; quantifying the error-class share in modern transformer parsers and the voting fix's precision on public multi-page corpora appears undone.

full_record.main_risk: Furniture varies in books with alternating recto/verso layouts; voting must handle two-phase periodicity or precision drops.

full_record.core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESis] Pan-sharpening errors are not neutral noise for detection: comparing detection on pan-sharpened inputs versus a dual-stream model consuming native panchromatic and multispectral separately will show the fused product both creates false positives at chroma-hallucination sites and misses objects whose spectral signature was averaged away, with a net measurable cost that grows for objects near the multispectral resolution limit.
full_record.falsifiable_prediction: [EXPECTED RESULT] Dual-stream native-resolution detection will beat pan-sharpened single-stream by at least 3 mAP points on small objects (under 3x multispectral GSD) while tying within 1 point on large objects; kill the idea if pan-sharpened input ties or wins on small objects, meaning hallucination is detection-neutral.
full_record.why_important: Operational feeds (defense, maritime, urgent response) are pan-sharpened by default at the provider level; if fusion hurts small-object detection, the standard delivery pipeline is destroying capability that native products retain.
full_record.why_possibly_novel: [MODEL SPECULATION / unverified] Pan-sharpening quality is evaluated with image metrics; a detection-outcome audit of fusion hallucination with object-size stratification appears missing.
full_record.minimal_falsification_experiment: On a public dataset providing native panchromatic and multispectral bands, train pan-sharpened-input and dual-stream detectors with matched capacity, and compare mAP stratified by object size relative to multispectral GSD.
full_record.main_risk: Dual-stream architectures introduce their own design choices; several fusion points must be tried to avoid attributing architecture effects to the input products.
full_record.community_default_belief: [MODEL SPECULATION] Pan-sharpened products are treated as strictly superior inputs because they look sharper and score well on perceptual metrics.
full_record.why_it_might_be_wrong: Detectors may be robust to chroma hallucination because they rely on panchromatic-derived edges, making fusion effects negligible.
full_record.fastest_falsification_experiment: Public data and model: SpaceNet catalogs with native band products and YOLOv8/Faster R-CNN; paired training runs in about 25 GPU-hours on one consumer GPU (~$50).

full_record.falsifiable_prediction: [EXPECTED RESULT] Above the saturation stratum, optical-only correlation with lidar reference will fall below half its unsaturated value, and SAR fusion will recover at least 30% of the saturated-stratum deficit while adding under 10% in the unsaturated stratum; kill the idea if optical accuracy is regime-flat (ratio above 0.8) or SAR gains are uniform across regimes.
full_record.why_important: Forest carbon markets and climate policy consume these maps; regime-blind aggregate metrics overstate reliability exactly in high-carbon dense forests where the stakes are highest.
full_record.why_possibly_novel: [MODEL SPECULATION / unverified] Spectral saturation is classical ecology-remote-sensing knowledge; a regime-stratified audit of modern deep regressors with a mechanism-confirming fusion test appears unassembled.

full_record.main_risk: Lidar footprint geolocation error and sparse sampling complicate stratified evaluation; footprint-level matching must be quality-filtered.

full_record.core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] A null model that knows only the season mapping (trained to transform between season appearances using historical unchanged areas, then thresholding residuals) will achieve a substantial fraction of published change-detection scores, and the fraction will vary widely across benchmarks, quantifying how much each benchmark actually tests change understanding versus seasonal normalization.

full_record.why_possibly_novel: [MODEL SPECULATION / unverified] Season-aware change methods exist; using a season-only null as a benchmark-auditing instrument with cross-benchmark comparison appears new.

full_record.main_risk: Benchmarks with tight acquisition-date matching will trivially defeat the null, so benchmark selection must span the date-gap spectrum for the heterogeneity claim.
full_record.community_default_belief: [MODEL SPECULATION] Benchmark F1 is read as change-understanding capability, with seasonal nuisance assumed subtracted by learned representations.
full_record.why_it_might_be_wrong: Labeled changes may be visually dramatic enough that even season-confused models find them, compressing the null-vs-SOTA gap for uninteresting reasons.

one_line_idea: Urbanization is nearly irreversible at monitoring timescales, and decoding land-cover time series under a monotonicity constraint removes temporal flicker while leaving accuracy unchanged, exploiting process physics that frame-independent models ignore.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Enforcing class-transition monotonicity (urban absorbing state) as a decoding constraint over the time series will eliminate most flicker and slightly improve per-date accuracy near transition dates, because the constraint is true of the underlying process; the transition-date estimates will also sharpen, measured against high-confidence construction records.

full_record.one_line_idea: Urbanization is nearly irreversible at monitoring timescales, and decoding land-cover time series under a monotonicity constraint removes temporal flicker while leaving accuracy unchanged, exploiting process physics that frame-independent models ignore.
full_record.problem: [KNOWN FACT] Per-date land-cover maps from independent inference flicker (pixels oscillate urban/non-urban across dates), forcing ad-hoc post-hoc smoothing; urban conversion, however, is a directional process that essentially never reverts within monitoring horizons.
full_record.core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Enforcing class-transition monotonicity (urban absorbing state) as a decoding constraint over the time series will eliminate most flicker and slightly improve per-date accuracy near transition dates, because the constraint is true of the underlying process; the transition-date estimates will also sharpen, measured against high-confidence construction records.
full_record.falsifiable_prediction: [EXPECTED RESULT] Monotone decoding will cut urban-class temporal flicker (reversal rate) by at least 80% while changing per-date accuracy by no worse than -0.5 points and improving transition-date MAE by at least 20%; kill the idea if accuracy drops more than 1.5 points or transition dating does not improve, meaning flicker was carrying real signal.
full_record.why_important: Urban growth statistics drive planning and climate models; flicker forces arbitrary smoothing choices that bias growth-rate estimates, while a process-true constraint is principled and parameter-free.
full_record.why_possibly_novel: [MODEL SPECULATION / unverified] Temporal smoothing is ubiquitous; framing irreversibility as a decodable absorbing-state constraint with transition-dating validation appears rare in the deep-learning era.
full_record.minimal_falsification_experiment: Run per-date inference on a public dense-time-series benchmark, apply monotone dynamic-programming decoding on urban classes, and evaluate flicker, per-date accuracy, and transition-date error against labels.
full_record.main_risk: Demolition-to-greenfield does occur (rare); the constraint needs an escape probability or it will propagate rare errors forward indefinitely.
full_record.community_default_belief: [MODEL SPECULATION] Temporal consistency is pursued with generic smoothing or recurrent models, not with process-specific transition structure.
full_record.why_it_might_be_wrong: Modern temporal architectures may already produce near-monotone outputs, leaving little flicker to remove.
full_record.fastest_falsification_experiment: Public data and model: Dynamic EarthNet daily time series with a U-TAE or Prithvi-based classifier; decoding experiments run in about 12 GPU-hours on one consumer GPU (~$25).

core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Gap-filling is a smoothness prior that suppresses genuine abrupt events occurring during unobserved windows, so change statistics computed from filled series are biased low, with the bias growing with gap fraction; the effect is quantifiable by artificially masking observations from nearly-complete series and measuring recovered change rates against the withheld truth.

full_record.core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Logical-anomaly detectability is governed by the ratio of anomaly context scale to method receptive field: patch-statistic methods will fail on logical anomalies at rates predictable from that ratio alone, implying benchmark aggregate scores conflate two capabilities that should be reported and engineered separately (local density modeling versus global composition modeling).
full_record.falsifiable_prediction: [EXPECTED RESULT] Across public methods, logical-anomaly AUROC will regress on context-to-receptive-field ratio with R^2 >= 0.5, while structural AUROC shows no such dependence (R^2 < 0.1); kill the idea if the ratio explains under 20% of logical-anomaly variance, meaning the two-class framing is wrong.
full_record.why_important: Factories buying 'anomaly detection' get a single score today; a validated two-capability decomposition with a predictive scaling variable would change procurement, benchmarking, and method design.
full_record.why_possibly_novel: [MODEL SPECULATION / unverified] The structural/logical split exists in benchmarks; the receptive-field scaling law that predicts the split's difficulty appears unformulated.
full_record.minimal_falsification_experiment: Measure effective receptive fields of public anomaly methods, compute per-anomaly context scales from annotations, and fit the cross-method regression on logical versus structural AUROC.
full_record.main_risk: Effective receptive field estimation is method-dependent and noisy for memory-bank approaches, requiring careful operationalization.
full_record.community_default_belief: [MODEL SPECULATION] Leaderboard aggregates are treated as total anomaly capability, with logical anomalies seen as a harder-but-same-kind problem.
full_record.why_it_might_be_wrong: Logical failures may be driven by feature semantics rather than geometry, breaking the receptive-field regression.
full_record.fastest_falsification_experiment: Public data and model: MVTec LOCO with PatchCore, PaDiM, and EfficientAD implementations from the public anomalib library; the study runs in about 10 GPU-hours on one consumer GPU (~$20).

core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] A large fraction of headline anomaly-detection AUROC depends on implicit spatial registration: applying small geometric perturbations (rotations up to 5 degrees, translations up to 5%, scale up to 3%) to test images will degrade memory-bank methods far more than reconstruction-based methods, and inserting an explicit pose-normalization front end will recover most of the loss, quantifying the registration share of performance.

one_line_idea: Surface defect visibility is BRDF-gated: many scratches and dents are invisible under any single illumination but detectable in multi-illumination stacks, and the invisible fraction is measurable, bounding what single-image inspection can ever achieve.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] For directional-texture surfaces there exists a substantial defect subpopulation whose single-light contrast is below detectability for any single light direction, but which photometric fusion across a few directions renders detectable; measuring detection as a function of illumination count therefore yields a saturating curve whose asymptote-versus-single-light gap is the physical bound on single-image inspection.

full_record.falsifiable_prediction: [EXPECTED RESULT] On multi-illumination captures, at least 15% of verified defects will be undetectable (below human and model detection) in every single-light image while detectable in fused stacks, with detection saturating by 4-6 light directions; kill the idea if the single-light-invisible fraction is under 4%, meaning illumination diversity is a marginal concern.
full_record.why_important: Vendors sell single-camera single-light systems on benchmark numbers; a measured physical bound would redirect hardware design (cheap multi-LED domes) and set honest expectations for miss rates.
full_record.why_possibly_novel: [MODEL SPECULATION / unverified] Photometric stereo inspection exists in niche systems; the population-level invisible-fraction measurement with a saturation curve appears unpublished.
full_record.minimal_falsification_experiment: Capture (or source) a multi-illumination defect dataset, verify defects physically, evaluate single-light versus fused detection across illumination counts, and estimate the invisible fraction with confidence intervals.
full_record.main_risk: Public multi-illumination industrial datasets are rare; a capture rig (a few hundred dollars of LEDs and a controller) plus sample parts is likely required.
full_record.community_default_belief: [MODEL SPECULATION] Missed defects are attributed to model weakness, fixable with more data, rather than to physical invisibility under the deployed illumination.
full_record.why_it_might_be_wrong: For matte surfaces the specular gating may be negligible, confining the result to glossy/machined finishes.

one_line_idea: Beam-hardening artifacts in industrial X-ray CT mimic porosity defects at geometry-predictable locations, and injecting a physics-computed artifact map as an input channel cuts false calls in casting inspection without any new labels.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] False-positive void detections cluster at physics-predictable artifact loci, and providing the detector with a simulated artifact-susceptibility map (computed by polychromatic forward projection through the part's CAD or reconstructed geometry) lets it discount artifact-consistent darkness, reducing false calls while preserving true porosity sensitivity.

full_record.problem: [KNOWN FACT] Polychromatic X-ray beams harden through thick metal sections, producing cupping and streak artifacts whose locations are deterministic given part geometry and scan setup; learned porosity detectors flag these dark artifacts as voids.
full_record.core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] False-positive void detections cluster at physics-predictable artifact loci, and providing the detector with a simulated artifact-susceptibility map (computed by polychromatic forward projection through the part's CAD or reconstructed geometry) lets it discount artifact-consistent darkness, reducing false calls while preserving true porosity sensitivity.
full_record.falsifiable_prediction: [EXPECTED RESULT] At matched true-positive rate, the artifact-map-conditioned model will cut false calls by at least 30%, and ablating the map will restore at least 80% of them; kill the idea if false-call reduction is under 10%, meaning detectors already separate artifacts from voids.
full_record.why_important: False calls drive re-inspection cost in foundries and erode trust in automated CT inspection; a physics side-channel fix requires no new annotation and is auditable by quality engineers.
full_record.why_possibly_novel: [MODEL SPECULATION / unverified] Beam-hardening correction is standard reconstruction practice; feeding residual artifact susceptibility to learned defect detectors appears unexplored.
full_record.minimal_falsification_experiment: Simulate polychromatic scans of parts with known void placements, train detectors with and without the susceptibility channel, and evaluate false-call rates at matched sensitivity on held-out geometries.
full_record.main_risk: Public industrial CT defect data is scarce; simulation-heavy validation invites the objection that real scanner artifacts differ, requiring at least one physical validation scan.
full_record.community_default_belief: [MODEL SPECULATION] Artifact handling is assumed to belong entirely to the reconstruction stage, with detection models expected to cope with residuals via data.
full_record.why_it_might_be_wrong: Modern iterative reconstruction may suppress artifacts sufficiently that residual false calls stem from other causes (scatter, noise).

full_record.why_important: Composite aerostructures and battery housings need subsurface inspection at line speed; establishing the temporal information law tells practitioners whether to invest in sequence capture and modeling or single-shot cameras.
full_record.why_possibly_novel: [MODEL SPECULATION / unverified] Thermographic signal processing has classical transforms; a controlled frame-vs-sequence learning comparison with depth-resolved physics validation appears missing.

full_record.why_it_might_be_wrong: Classical compressed representations (polynomial fits of log-decay) may already capture the dynamics, letting frame-based models on those features tie sequence models.

one_line_idea: Monocular depth underwater is not scale-ambiguous the way it is in air: wavelength-dependent attenuation provides an absolute range cue, so a lightweight attenuation-reading head can convert relative depth maps into metric depth without stereo or sonar.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] A small head on a frozen relative-depth backbone that estimates global metric scale from red-to-green attenuation statistics recovers metric depth without geometric cues, because water itself acts as an absolute rangefinder that air lacks.

full_record.one_line_idea: Monocular depth underwater is not scale-ambiguous the way it is in air: wavelength-dependent attenuation provides an absolute range cue, so a lightweight attenuation-reading head can convert relative depth maps into metric depth without stereo or sonar.
full_record.problem: [KNOWN FACT] Monocular depth estimation in air recovers only relative depth up to an unknown global scale because pinhole projection is scale-invariant; underwater, per-channel light attenuation ties an object's color shift to its absolute optical path length, and public underwater RGB-D data exists.
full_record.core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] A small head on a frozen relative-depth backbone that estimates global metric scale from red-to-green attenuation statistics recovers metric depth without geometric cues, because water itself acts as an absolute rangefinder that air lacks.
full_record.falsifiable_prediction: [EXPECTED RESULT] On held-out FLSea dives, an attenuation-conditioned scale head will cut median absolute metric-depth error to below 60% of the best constant-per-dive scale baseline, with per-scene scale estimates correlating with true scale at Spearman rho >= 0.6; kill the idea if error reduction is under 15%, if rho < 0.3, or if more than 80% of the gain disappears when fit and test dives have different water types.
full_record.why_important: Metric monocular depth would let low-cost AUVs and diver cameras do collision avoidance and photogrammetric measurement without stereo rigs or active sonar, exploiting a physical cue that only exists underwater.
full_record.why_possibly_novel: [MODEL SPECULATION / unverified] Underwater depth work treats attenuation as a nuisance to correct or relies on geometry alone; using attenuation explicitly as the absolute-scale oracle for monocular depth appears untested.
full_record.minimal_falsification_experiment: Fit a scale head on FLSea training dives using per-image channel-ratio statistics against metric ground truth; evaluate scale-factor recovery and metric error on held-out dives against constant-scale and least-squares oracle-scale baselines.
full_record.main_risk: Artificial lighting and albedo variation may confound channel ratios enough that the scale signal is only usable in sunlit shallow water.
full_record.community_default_belief: [MODEL SPECULATION] Practitioners assume metric monocular depth requires known camera height, stereo, or learned scene-size priors, and treat underwater color shift purely as degradation to remove.
full_record.why_it_might_be_wrong: Scene albedo diversity may make channel-ratio statistics too noisy for per-scene scale estimation, leaving only a weak dataset-average prior that the constant baseline already captures.
full_record.fastest_falsification_experiment: Public data and model: FLSea underwater RGB-D sequences with a frozen Depth Anything relative-depth backbone plus a small MLP scale head; fitting and held-out evaluation is under 8 GPU-hours on one consumer GPU (~$12).

one_line_idea: Wreck and boulder detectors on multibeam bathymetry silently overfit the arbitrary hillshade rendering azimuth, missing targets whose long axis aligns with the artificial light; multi-azimuth rendering or gradient-native inputs make detection azimuth-invariant.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] A detector trained on single-azimuth hillshades encodes that azimuth as a shading prior, so recall varies periodically with test-time render azimuth (troughs where target long axes align with the light direction), and training over multiple azimuths or on DEM gradients directly removes the dependence at no accuracy cost.

full_record.one_line_idea: Wreck and boulder detectors on multibeam bathymetry silently overfit the arbitrary hillshade rendering azimuth, missing targets whose long axis aligns with the artificial light; multi-azimuth rendering or gradient-native inputs make detection azimuth-invariant.
full_record.problem: [KNOWN FACT] Multibeam bathymetry grids are conventionally rendered as hillshaded relief under one arbitrary artificial sun azimuth before being fed to detectors; hillshading is a deterministic function of the elevation grid and the chosen azimuth, and public bathymetry plus wreck registries exist.
full_record.core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] A detector trained on single-azimuth hillshades encodes that azimuth as a shading prior, so recall varies periodically with test-time render azimuth (troughs where target long axes align with the light direction), and training over multiple azimuths or on DEM gradients directly removes the dependence at no accuracy cost.
full_record.falsifiable_prediction: [EXPECTED RESULT] Single-azimuth-trained detector recall will vary by >= 15 points peak-to-trough as the test hillshade azimuth rotates through 360 degrees, and multi-azimuth training or gradient-native inputs will cut that variation to <= 5 points at equal mean recall; kill the idea if single-azimuth variation is < 5 points, or if the azimuth-invariant variants lose > 3 points mean recall.
full_record.why_important: Hydrographic offices and marine archaeologists screen bathymetry at scale; an azimuth-dependent detector systematically misses real wrecks because of an arbitrary visualization choice, and the fix is free once measured.
full_record.why_possibly_novel: [MODEL SPECULATION / unverified] Hillshade-based deep detection on bathymetry is common practice, but a quantified periodic recall law tied to the rendering azimuth and a rendering-side invariance fix appear untested for seabed targets.
full_record.minimal_falsification_experiment: Build wreck/boulder chips from public bathymetry grids and wreck registry positions; render each chip at 8 azimuths; train detectors under single- and multi-azimuth regimes and measure recall as a function of test azimuth and target orientation.
full_record.main_risk: Registry positional errors may blur target orientation statistics, weakening the predicted trough alignment even if the azimuth sensitivity is real.
full_record.community_default_belief: [MODEL SPECULATION] Practitioners treat hillshade azimuth as a cosmetic visualization parameter with no bearing on trained-model behavior.
full_record.why_it_might_be_wrong: Modern detectors with strong augmentation may already be sufficiently shading-invariant, making the measured variation small.
full_record.fastest_falsification_experiment: Public data and model: NOAA NCEI multibeam bathymetry with AWOIS wreck locations and a YOLOv8 detector; chip extraction, 8-azimuth rendering, and both training regimes are under 10 GPU-hours on one consumer GPU (~$15).

one_line_idea: Under a shrinking photon budget, microscopy classes fail in an order predicted by the spatial scale and contrast of their diagnostic features (a Rose-criterion ordering), making low-dose robustness a per-class physical quantity rather than a model property.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] As synthetic dose reduction deepens, per-class accuracy of a fixed classifier collapses in an order determined by each class's diagnostic spatial-frequency content: fine-textured phenotypes collapse first and coarse-morphology phenotypes last, with the ordering stable across architectures because it is set by optics, not by learning.

full_record.one_line_idea: Under a shrinking photon budget, microscopy classes fail in an order predicted by the spatial scale and contrast of their diagnostic features (a Rose-criterion ordering), making low-dose robustness a per-class physical quantity rather than a model property.
full_record.problem: [KNOWN FACT] Fluorescence imaging noise is photon-limited (Poisson), dose reduction to limit phototoxicity is routine, and the Rose criterion ties feature detectability to contrast, feature size, and photon count.
full_record.core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] As synthetic dose reduction deepens, per-class accuracy of a fixed classifier collapses in an order determined by each class's diagnostic spatial-frequency content: fine-textured phenotypes collapse first and coarse-morphology phenotypes last, with the ordering stable across architectures because it is set by optics, not by learning.
full_record.falsifiable_prediction: [EXPECTED RESULT] The rank correlation between per-class collapse dose and a physics-derived detectability score (feature scale times contrast, computed from held-out high-dose images) will be >= 0.6, and class orderings will agree across two architectures at Kendall tau >= 0.5; kill the idea if the correlation is < 0.3 or if orderings disagree across architectures (tau < 0.2).
full_record.why_important: Imaging scientists could budget light dose per assay from physics alone, predicting which phenotypes remain readable at low phototoxicity without retraining or recollecting data.
full_record.why_possibly_novel: [MODEL SPECULATION / unverified] Low-dose robustness is usually reported as a single dataset-level curve; a per-class collapse-ordering law grounded in the Rose criterion, with architecture-independence as an explicit test, appears untested.
full_record.minimal_falsification_experiment: Apply calibrated Poisson dose scaling to a public high-SNR phenotype-classification set, train two classifier families, measure per-class collapse doses, and correlate them with detectability scores computed from an independent split.
full_record.main_risk: Diagnostic-feature scale must be estimated from data, risking circularity unless the detectability score is computed from splits and channels disjoint from evaluation.
full_record.community_default_belief: [MODEL SPECULATION] The community treats low-dose degradation as a uniform noise-robustness property of the model, to be fixed by denoisers or augmentation, not as a class-structured optical limit.
full_record.why_it_might_be_wrong: Deep classifiers may rely on distributed features whose effective scale differs from the visually diagnostic structures, breaking the physics-derived ordering.
full_record.fastest_falsification_experiment: Public data and model: BBBC021 mechanism-of-action fluorescence images with ResNet-50 and a small ViT; Poisson dose sweeps, two trainings, and evaluation are under 10 GPU-hours on one consumer GPU (~$15).

one_line_idea: 3D microscopy segmentation benchmarks are quietly dominated by shallow, aberration-free planes: refractive-index mismatch degrades the PSF with imaging depth, and depth-stratified scoring plus PSF-matched augmentation exposes and partially closes a gap that headline numbers hide.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Published 3D nucleus/cell segmentation scores are dominated by shallow planes where the PSF is near-nominal; per-instance accuracy declines systematically with depth, and physics-matched depth-dependent PSF augmentation at train time recovers a substantial part of the deep-plane gap while depth-uniform blur augmentation does not.

full_record.one_line_idea: 3D microscopy segmentation benchmarks are quietly dominated by shallow, aberration-free planes: refractive-index mismatch degrades the PSF with imaging depth, and depth-stratified scoring plus PSF-matched augmentation exposes and partially closes a gap that headline numbers hide.
full_record.problem: [KNOWN FACT] Imaging into aqueous samples with immersion objectives creates depth-dependent spherical aberration from refractive-index mismatch; the PSF broadening with depth is computable from Gibson-Lanni-type optical models.
full_record.core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Published 3D nucleus/cell segmentation scores are dominated by shallow planes where the PSF is near-nominal; per-instance accuracy declines systematically with depth, and physics-matched depth-dependent PSF augmentation at train time recovers a substantial part of the deep-plane gap while depth-uniform blur augmentation does not.
full_record.falsifiable_prediction: [EXPECTED RESULT] Depth-stratified evaluation will show deep-stratum instance F1 at least 10 points below the shallow stratum on at least two public 3D datasets, and depth-dependent PSF augmentation will recover >= 40% of that gap versus <= 15% for strength-matched uniform Gaussian blur; kill the idea if the depth gap is < 4 points or if uniform blur matches PSF-matched augmentation within 2 points.
full_record.why_important: Deep-tissue quantification is exactly where 3D imaging is scientifically valuable; if benchmarks reward shallow-plane performance, method rankings are misleading for the use case that matters.
full_record.why_possibly_novel: [MODEL SPECULATION / unverified] Depth-dependent aberration is standard optics knowledge, but treating imaging depth as a first-class evaluation stratum for learned 3D segmenters, with a physics-matched augmentation control, appears untested.
full_record.minimal_falsification_experiment: Stratify existing 3D benchmark ground truth by z-position; evaluate public StarDist-3D/Cellpose checkpoints per stratum; retrain once with Gibson-Lanni depth-dependent PSF augmentation and once with uniform blur; compare stratified recovery.
full_record.main_risk: Some benchmarks were acquired with well-matched immersion media, so the natural depth gap may be small there and the audit must select datasets by acquisition metadata.
full_record.community_default_belief: [MODEL SPECULATION] The community reports single pooled scores for 3D segmentation and treats z-degradation as dataset noise rather than as a systematic, physically modelable evaluation axis.
full_record.why_it_might_be_wrong: Deep-plane degradation may be dominated by scattering and photon loss rather than aberration, in which case PSF-matched augmentation would not outperform generic blur.
full_record.fastest_falsification_experiment: Public data and model: Cell Tracking Challenge 3D fluorescence sets (e.g., Fluo-N3DH-CE) and BBBC 3D sets with public StarDist-3D/Cellpose checkpoints; stratified evaluation plus one retraining is under 12 GPU-hours on one consumer GPU (~$18).

one_line_idea: Learned single-molecule localization networks hit a breakdown emitter density set by PSF-overlap statistics: the breakdown point scales predictably with PSF width and barely moves with more training data — an optics-set capability ceiling.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] The density at which a learned localizer's efficiency collapses is governed by the probability of multi-emitter PSF-overlap events exceeding the network's local disambiguation capacity, so breakdown density scales approximately as the inverse square of PSF width, and a tenfold increase in training frames shifts it only marginally.

full_record.one_line_idea: Learned single-molecule localization networks hit a breakdown emitter density set by PSF-overlap statistics: the breakdown point scales predictably with PSF width and barely moves with more training data — an optics-set capability ceiling.
full_record.problem: [KNOWN FACT] Single-molecule localization microscopy reconstructs super-resolved images from sparse blinking emitters; deep localizers extend to higher emitter densities than classical fitting, and the public SMLM challenge provides calibrated simulators and benchmarks.
full_record.core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] The density at which a learned localizer's efficiency collapses is governed by the probability of multi-emitter PSF-overlap events exceeding the network's local disambiguation capacity, so breakdown density scales approximately as the inverse square of PSF width, and a tenfold increase in training frames shifts it only marginally.
full_record.falsifiable_prediction: [EXPECTED RESULT] Across simulated PSF widths spanning a factor of two, the measured breakdown density (efficiency falling below 0.5) will scale with a fitted exponent in [-2.6, -1.4] versus PSF width, and 10x more training frames will move breakdown density by < 20%; kill the idea if the exponent falls outside [-3.5, -0.8] or if 10x data moves the breakdown by > 60%.
full_record.why_important: Microscopists could compute the maximum usable labeling density per optical setup before an experiment, and method developers would know when gains must come from optics (PSF engineering) rather than from bigger models or datasets.
full_record.why_possibly_novel: [MODEL SPECULATION / unverified] Deep-SMLM papers report density robustness empirically per method; an explicit overlap-statistics scaling law with a data-scaling null control appears untested.
full_record.minimal_falsification_experiment: Use the SMLM challenge simulator to generate density sweeps at several PSF widths; train and evaluate DECODE at each grid point; fit the breakdown-density scaling exponent; rerun one grid point with 10x training frames as the data-scaling control.
full_record.main_risk: Training many DECODE instances is compute-heavy, so reduced-size proxies are needed and may shift the fitted exponent.
full_record.community_default_belief: [MODEL SPECULATION] The community narrative is that higher-density performance is primarily a modeling problem that better architectures and more simulation data will keep improving.
full_record.why_it_might_be_wrong: Networks may exploit temporal blinking correlations across frames, partially decoupling breakdown density from single-frame overlap statistics.
full_record.fastest_falsification_experiment: Public data and model: SMLM 2016 challenge datasets and simulator with the public DECODE codebase; a reduced-resolution density-PSF grid is under 20 GPU-hours on one consumer GPU (~$30).

one_line_idea: Tissue folds have an exact physical signature that no other artifact shares — near-doubled optical density in both stain channels with an unchanged stain ratio — so a label-free stain-physics fold detector can inoculate slide-level models against a dominant failure mode.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] A label-free detector flagging regions with approximately 2x local-background optical density in both deconvolved stain channels and an unchanged H-to-E ratio will match supervised artifact-QC tools at fold detection, and masking its detections will recover much of the slide-level accuracy lost on fold-contaminated slides.

full_record.one_line_idea: Tissue folds have an exact physical signature that no other artifact shares — near-doubled optical density in both stain channels with an unchanged stain ratio — so a label-free stain-physics fold detector can inoculate slide-level models against a dominant failure mode.
full_record.problem: [KNOWN FACT] Tissue folds arise when a section doubles over during mounting, locally doubling section thickness; under Beer-Lambert absorption, doubled thickness approximately doubles optical density in both hematoxylin and eosin channels while preserving their ratio, unlike genuinely dense tissue where the stain ratio shifts.
full_record.core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] A label-free detector flagging regions with approximately 2x local-background optical density in both deconvolved stain channels and an unchanged H-to-E ratio will match supervised artifact-QC tools at fold detection, and masking its detections will recover much of the slide-level accuracy lost on fold-contaminated slides.
full_record.falsifiable_prediction: [EXPECTED RESULT] The OD-doubling detector will agree with a supervised QC tool's fold flags at Cohen's kappa >= 0.7 region-level, and masking will recover >= 50% of the slide-level AUC drop measured between fold-contaminated and clean slides for a fixed MIL classifier; kill the idea if kappa < 0.4 or if AUC recovery is < 15%.
full_record.why_important: Folds are among the most common slide artifacts in routine labs; a zero-label physics detector is deployable everywhere, unlike QC models that need artifact annotations per site and scanner.
full_record.why_possibly_novel: [MODEL SPECULATION / unverified] Artifact QC is normally treated as a supervised or heuristic texture problem; deriving a fold detector directly from Beer-Lambert doubling with a stain-ratio invariance test appears untested.
full_record.minimal_falsification_experiment: Run stain deconvolution and the OD-ratio rule on public slides flagged by HistoQC as folded; compute region-level agreement; then evaluate a public CLAM checkpoint with and without fold masking on contaminated versus clean subsets.
full_record.main_risk: Thick-but-unfolded regions and coverslip debris may partially mimic the doubling signature, requiring a tolerance band that trades precision against recall.
full_record.community_default_belief: [MODEL SPECULATION] The community default is that artifact robustness comes from training-time augmentation or learned QC classifiers, not from closed-form stain physics.
full_record.why_it_might_be_wrong: MIL classifiers may already attend away from folds, making the measurable AUC recovery small even when detection works.
full_record.fastest_falsification_experiment: Public data and model: CAMELYON16/TCGA slides with the public HistoQC tool and a public CLAM checkpoint; deconvolution, rule evaluation, and masked re-inference are under 8 GPU-hours on one consumer GPU (~$12).

full_record.problem: [KNOWN FACT] Frozen sections suffer ice-crystal formation, compression, and inferior staining compared to FFPE; TCGA publicly provides both frozen and FFPE slides for many of the same cases, and intraoperative AI must run on frozen sections.
full_record.core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] For a fixed pathology foundation encoder, within-case cross-preparation disagreement is systematic and task-structured: nuclear-texture-dependent predictions degrade far more than tissue-architecture-dependent predictions on the same paired slides, and per-case degradation scales with a measurable ice-artifact severity score.
full_record.falsifiable_prediction: [EXPECTED RESULT] Cross-preparation within-case prediction agreement will be at least 15 points lower for a nuclear-texture probe than for a tissue-architecture probe on the same paired cohort, and per-case degradation will correlate with an ice-artifact severity proxy at Spearman rho >= 0.4; kill the idea if the task-structure difference is < 5 points or if rho < 0.15.
full_record.why_important: Intraoperative deployment is the highest-stakes pathology AI setting; knowing which task families survive freezing artifacts, and predicting per-slide reliability from artifact severity, determines what is safe to deploy.
full_record.why_possibly_novel: [MODEL SPECULATION / unverified] Frozen-vs-FFPE degradation is reported anecdotally as a domain gap; exploiting TCGA's within-case pairing to measure a task-structured gap law with an artifact-severity predictor appears untested.
full_record.minimal_falsification_experiment: Select TCGA cases having both DX (FFPE) and TS/BS (frozen) slides; run a public pathology foundation encoder with linear probes for one texture task and one architecture task; compare within-case agreement and correlate with a lacunae-statistics ice-severity proxy.
full_record.main_risk: Frozen and FFPE slides of a case sample different tissue blocks, so genuine spatial heterogeneity contributes to disagreement and must be bounded with within-preparation controls.
full_record.community_default_belief: [MODEL SPECULATION] The community treats the frozen-section gap as one scalar domain shift to be closed with style transfer, rather than as a structured, per-task, per-severity quantity.

full_record.one_line_idea: Newsprint halftone screens are periodic and FFT-detectable, so per-page physics-based descreening — notching the measured screen frequency before recognition — beats generic learned denoising for OCR on scanned newspapers at near-zero compute.
full_record.problem: [KNOWN FACT] Printed photographs and shaded regions in newspapers are halftone screens: periodic dot lattices with a measurable ruling and angle; rescanning aliases these lattices into moire and dot noise that overlaps thin text strokes, and public newspaper scan corpora are enormous.
full_record.core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] OCR errors on scanned newsprint concentrate where halftone spectral energy overlaps stroke frequencies, and a per-page descreen filter built by detecting lattice peaks in the Fourier spectrum and notching them removes this error mass more effectively than blind learned denoisers at matched runtime, because the artifact is exactly periodic.
full_record.falsifiable_prediction: [EXPECTED RESULT] On halftone-adjacent text lines, FFT-notch descreening will cut character error rate by >= 20% relative to no preprocessing and beat a public blind denoiser at matched runtime by >= 5% relative; kill the idea if the improvement is < 5% relative or if the blind denoiser matches the notch filter within 2% relative.
full_record.why_important: Mass digitization projects (national libraries, archives) OCR billions of newspaper pages with fixed pipelines; a closed-form preprocessing gain at CPU cost translates into corpus-scale text-quality improvement.
full_record.why_possibly_novel: [MODEL SPECULATION / unverified] Descreening exists in prepress tooling, but quantifying halftone-caused OCR error concentration and testing physics-notch filtering against learned denoisers for recognition (not visual quality) appears untested.
full_record.minimal_falsification_experiment: Simulate halftone printing and rescanning on born-digital pages for exact ground truth, plus a spot check on real newspaper scans; classify text lines by halftone proximity; measure CER under no preprocessing, FFT-notch descreening, and a public blind denoiser at matched runtime.
full_record.main_risk: Real scans mix multiple degradations (ink spread, yellowing), so the halftone-specific share of errors may be smaller in the wild than in simulation.
full_record.community_default_belief: [MODEL SPECULATION] The community default is that generic learned enhancement subsumes any hand-built preprocessing, making physics-specific filters obsolete.
full_record.why_it_might_be_wrong: Modern recognizers may already be robust to periodic dot noise through training-data diversity, leaving little error mass for descreening to recover.
full_record.fastest_falsification_experiment: Public data and model: Library of Congress Chronicling America page scans and halftone-simulated DocBank pages with public Tesseract and TrOCR checkpoints; filtering plus OCR over a few thousand lines is under 4 GPU-hours on one consumer GPU (~$6).

full_record.problem: [KNOWN FACT] Text legibility is limited by sampling: strokes narrower than about two pixels cannot be represented without aliasing; document benchmarks confound scan DPI, font size, and content, so reported low-quality robustness mixes these factors.
full_record.core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] For modern recognizers, character error rate is chiefly a function of physical glyph sampling (x-height in pixels), so curves measured across fonts, documents, and recognizers collapse onto a single master curve whose knee location is set by stroke-width sampling, and benchmark difficulty is largely explained by where items sit on this curve.

full_record.why_important: A validated master curve turns 'this scan is too low quality' into a measurable per-item quantity, enabling principled triage of digitization backlogs and honest cross-benchmark difficulty comparison.
full_record.why_possibly_novel: [MODEL SPECULATION / unverified] Robustness papers sweep noise and blur but conflate resolution with content; an explicit sampling-theory master-curve claim with a collapse test across fonts and recognizers appears untested.

full_record.main_risk: Recognizer language priors partially compensate for illegible glyphs, which could flatten the knee differently per model and per text predictability.
full_record.community_default_belief: [MODEL SPECULATION] The community reports robustness against DPI or generic 'low quality' labels, implicitly assuming resolution difficulty is model-specific rather than a shared physical curve.

one_line_idea: Document VQA models often answer forms from layout-template priors instead of reading: swapping a field's printed value in place (font-matched, pixel-consistent) leaves a measurable fraction of answers stuck at the old value, concentrated on frequent templates.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] A calibrated in-place value-substitution test (rendering a different but format-valid value into the same field with matched font and background) will show that current models frequently return the original or a prior-typical value instead of the printed one, with the failure rate substantially higher on high-frequency templates than on rare layouts.

full_record.one_line_idea: Document VQA models often answer forms from layout-template priors instead of reading: swapping a field's printed value in place (font-matched, pixel-consistent) leaves a measurable fraction of answers stuck at the old value, concentrated on frequent templates.
full_record.problem: [KNOWN FACT] Document VQA benchmarks contain recurring form and invoice templates in which answer fields sit at predictable positions with predictable value formats, so a model can score well by mapping question type to field position and emitting a prior-typical token.
full_record.core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] A calibrated in-place value-substitution test (rendering a different but format-valid value into the same field with matched font and background) will show that current models frequently return the original or a prior-typical value instead of the printed one, with the failure rate substantially higher on high-frequency templates than on rare layouts.
full_record.falsifiable_prediction: [EXPECTED RESULT] On edited fields where the model was previously correct, at least 20% of answers will fail to flip to the newly printed value for a strong public model, and the flip-failure rate will be at least 2x higher on high-frequency templates; kill the idea if flip-failure is < 8% overall or shows no template-frequency dependence (ratio < 1.2x).
full_record.why_important: Production document AI reads values that change across document versions; a model answering from template priors silently returns stale values — an unmonitored, high-cost failure class that benchmark accuracy cannot see.
full_record.why_possibly_novel: [MODEL SPECULATION / unverified] Perturbation audits exist for natural-image VQA, but a pixel-consistent in-place value-substitution protocol measuring reading fidelity versus template priors on document VQA appears untested.
full_record.minimal_falsification_experiment: Auto-render font-matched substitutions on a few hundred DocVQA/FUNSD fields (estimate font and background locally), rerun public Donut and LayoutLMv3 pipelines, and measure answer-flip rates stratified by template frequency.
full_record.main_risk: Imperfect font matching introduces edit artifacts that models might detect, confounding 'did not read' with 'read the artifact'; an artifact-only control edit is required.
full_record.community_default_belief: [MODEL SPECULATION] The community treats DocVQA accuracy as evidence of reading ability, assuming positional priors are a minor contributor for state-of-the-art models.
full_record.why_it_might_be_wrong: End-to-end models with strong OCR backbones may genuinely read edited values, yielding flip-failure rates below the kill threshold — which would itself be a useful negative result.
full_record.fastest_falsification_experiment: Public data and model: DocVQA and FUNSD with public Donut and LayoutLMv3 checkpoints; editing and re-inference over about 1k fields is under 4 GPU-hours on one consumer GPU (~$6).

one_line_idea: Professionally typeset pages sit on a hidden baseline grid; estimating the grid from projection-profile autocorrelation and snapping line hypotheses to it removes the merge/split errors that dominate dense-layout parsing, with no learning required.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] A post-processing layer that estimates per-block baseline period and phase, then vetoes line hypotheses inconsistent with the grid (merges spanning two periods, splits at off-grid positions), removes a large share of line-level errors of any underlying detector, with gains concentrated on dense layouts and vanishing on sparse ones — a mechanism-specificity signature.

full_record.problem: [KNOWN FACT] Typesetting systems place text on regular baseline grids (near-constant leading within blocks); line-detection errors on dense multi-column pages are dominated by merged adjacent lines and split tall glyphs, and the grid period is recoverable from autocorrelation of horizontal projection profiles.
full_record.core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] A post-processing layer that estimates per-block baseline period and phase, then vetoes line hypotheses inconsistent with the grid (merges spanning two periods, splits at off-grid positions), removes a large share of line-level errors of any underlying detector, with gains concentrated on dense layouts and vanishing on sparse ones — a mechanism-specificity signature.
full_record.falsifiable_prediction: [EXPECTED RESULT] Grid snapping will remove >= 40% of merge/split line errors on dense pages (newspapers, two-column academic) while altering < 2% of correct detections, and gains will shrink toward zero on sparse layouts; kill the idea if merge/split removal is < 15% or if correct-detection damage exceeds 5%.
full_record.why_important: Line-level structure errors propagate into reading order, table extraction, and LLM document ingestion; a deterministic typographic constraint that fixes them costs nothing at inference and stacks with any detector.
full_record.why_possibly_novel: [MODEL SPECULATION / unverified] Layout post-processing is usually learned or heuristic per system; an explicit baseline-grid estimator with a snap-and-veto rule evaluated by error-class accounting appears untested on modern benchmarks.

full_record.main_risk: Pages mixing multiple leading values within a block (footnotes, display math) can defeat a single-period grid model and require piecewise estimation.
full_record.community_default_belief: [MODEL SPECULATION] The community default is that better detectors and more training data are the path to fixing line errors, treating typography as latent structure the network should learn implicitly.
full_record.why_it_might_be_wrong: Modern detectors may already internalize grid regularity, leaving too few grid-inconsistent errors for the post-processor to matter.
full_record.fastest_falsification_experiment: Public data and model: DocLayNet and PubLayNet with a public DiT or Faster R-CNN layout checkpoint; post-processing and error accounting are under 3 GPU-hours on one consumer GPU (~$5).

core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Pairwise transfer degradation between layout datasets is largely explained by divergence in layout-grammar statistics (region-type transition matrices, column-count distributions, region position/aspect statistics), and visual-domain distance adds little predictive power once grammar distance is controlled.

full_record.why_it_might_be_wrong: Grammar and visual distances are correlated across real collections, so disentangling them may need matched-visual synthetic controls that weaken external validity.

one_line_idea: Born-digital PDFs carry exact vector primitives (rules, paths, glyph boxes) that pixel-based table models throw away by re-rasterizing; a primitive-aware input stream recovers borderless and hairline-ruled structure that no practical raster resolution restores.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Feeding parsed vector primitives (line segments, glyph bounding boxes) as an auxiliary input stream to a table-structure model improves structure accuracy specifically on thin-ruled and borderless tables, and the gain cannot be matched by raising raster resolution at equal or greater compute — because the information is lost to sampling, not to model capacity.

full_record.one_line_idea: Born-digital PDFs carry exact vector primitives (rules, paths, glyph boxes) that pixel-based table models throw away by re-rasterizing; a primitive-aware input stream recovers borderless and hairline-ruled structure that no practical raster resolution restores.
full_record.problem: [KNOWN FACT] Most production documents are born-digital PDFs whose drawing commands specify rules, cell borders, and glyph placements exactly; standard document AI rasterizes pages and re-detects that structure from pixels, where hairline rules alias or vanish at common working resolutions.
full_record.core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Feeding parsed vector primitives (line segments, glyph bounding boxes) as an auxiliary input stream to a table-structure model improves structure accuracy specifically on thin-ruled and borderless tables, and the gain cannot be matched by raising raster resolution at equal or greater compute — because the information is lost to sampling, not to model capacity.
full_record.falsifiable_prediction: [EXPECTED RESULT] On rule-weight-stratified PubTables-1M subsets, a primitive-augmented model will improve structure TEDS by >= 4 points on hairline and borderless strata while a 2x-resolution pixel-only model gains <= 2 points at higher compute; kill the idea if primitive gains are < 1.5 points or if the resolution increase matches them at comparable cost.
full_record.why_important: Enterprise document extraction overwhelmingly processes born-digital PDFs; exploiting the native vector substrate is a free accuracy and compute win that current raster-first pipelines structurally forgo.
full_record.why_possibly_novel: [MODEL SPECULATION / unverified] Hybrid text+layout models use OCR tokens, but injecting the drawing-command geometry itself (rules and paths) as a first-class model input with a sampling-theory framing appears untested.

full_record.main_risk: PDF generators vary wildly in how they encode rules (strokes, filled rects, images), so the primitive parser needs normalization that could leak engineering effort into the comparison.
full_record.community_default_belief: [MODEL SPECULATION] The community default is that scaling image resolution and model capacity subsumes structured inputs, so raster-only pipelines are considered asymptotically sufficient.
full_record.why_it_might_be_wrong: For most real tables, whitespace and text alignment may carry enough structure that primitives add little beyond the hairline edge cases.
full_record.fastest_falsification_experiment: Public data and model: PubTables-1M (built from PDFs with word and structure annotations) with the public Table Transformer (TATR); primitive extraction plus one subset training is under 16 GPU-hours on one consumer GPU (~$24).

one_line_idea: Homogeneous industrial surfaces are stationary random textures, so spectral whitening — flattening the normal class's estimated power spectrum — is the physically matched preprocessing for texture anomaly detection, lifting patch-based detectors selectively on texture categories.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Whitening images with a filter derived from the normal class's average power spectrum amplifies statistical deviations relative to background and improves anomaly scoring on stationary-texture categories while leaving object categories unchanged or slightly degraded — a category-selective gain predicted by the stationarity assumption itself.

full_record.one_line_idea: Homogeneous industrial surfaces are stationary random textures, so spectral whitening — flattening the normal class's estimated power spectrum — is the physically matched preprocessing for texture anomaly detection, lifting patch-based detectors selectively on texture categories.
full_record.problem: [KNOWN FACT] Many inspected surfaces (fabric, carpet, wood, leather, foam) are approximately stationary random fields; anomalies are local violations of stationarity, and patch-embedding anomaly detectors compare features whose statistics are dominated by the texture's autocorrelation structure.
full_record.core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Whitening images with a filter derived from the normal class's average power spectrum amplifies statistical deviations relative to background and improves anomaly scoring on stationary-texture categories while leaving object categories unchanged or slightly degraded — a category-selective gain predicted by the stationarity assumption itself.
full_record.falsifiable_prediction: [EXPECTED RESULT] Spectral whitening will raise image-level AUROC on MVTec AD texture categories by >= 1.5 points mean for PatchCore and PaDiM while changing object categories by within +-0.5 points, and per-category gains will correlate with a measured stationarity index at Spearman rho >= 0.5; kill the idea if the mean texture gain is < 0.5 points or if gains show no stationarity correlation (rho < 0.2).
full_record.why_important: A closed-form preprocessing step that provably targets texture categories closes part of the texture-object performance split on industrial benchmarks and costs microseconds per image in deployment.
full_record.why_possibly_novel: [MODEL SPECULATION / unverified] Whitening is classical signal processing, but deriving it from the nominal class spectrum as an anomaly-detection preprocessing with a stationarity-selectivity prediction appears untested on modern benchmarks.
full_record.minimal_falsification_experiment: Estimate per-category normal power spectra, build whitening filters, rerun PatchCore and PaDiM through anomalib, compute per-category stationarity indices, and test the gain-selectivity correlation.
full_record.main_risk: ImageNet-pretrained backbones may internally decorrelate textures already, absorbing the whitening effect into a null result.
full_record.community_default_belief: [MODEL SPECULATION] The community treats preprocessing as obsolete for deep anomaly detection, expecting backbones and memory banks to handle texture statistics implicitly.
full_record.why_it_might_be_wrong: Whitening also amplifies sensor noise, which could raise false-positive scores on high-ISO captures and cancel the theoretical gain.
full_record.fastest_falsification_experiment: Public data and model: MVTec AD and VisA with public PatchCore and PaDiM implementations from anomalib; the full sweep is under 6 GPU-hours on one consumer GPU (~$9).

full_record.one_line_idea: Tide height at acquisition time is exactly computable from harmonic models, yet coastal change detection treats intertidal exposure as scene change; tide-stage-aware pairing or conditioning removes a dominant class of false coastal 'changes' at zero labeling cost.
full_record.problem: [KNOWN FACT] Intertidal zones flood and expose on tidal cycles; satellites sample quasi-random tidal stages; tide height at any coastal location and time is predictable from public harmonic tide models, and public optical archives densely cover coastlines.
full_record.core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] A large share of detected coastline and coastal-change events between image pairs is explained by tidal-stage difference alone, so matching pairs by tidal stage or feeding predicted tide height as a conditioning input removes most of these false events while preserving sensitivity to genuine change.
full_record.falsifiable_prediction: [EXPECTED RESULT] On stable coastal strips, flagged-change area will increase monotonically with absolute tide-height difference (Spearman rho >= 0.6), and tide-stage matching or conditioning will cut the false change-event rate by >= 50% at unchanged recall on injected genuine changes; kill the idea if flagged change is tide-insensitive (rho < 0.2) or if false-event reduction is < 15%.
full_record.why_important: Coastal monitoring (erosion, construction, aquaculture) is a major operational use of free satellite imagery, and a deterministic astronomical covariate that halves false alarms costs nothing to compute.
full_record.why_possibly_novel: [MODEL SPECULATION / unverified] Tide correction is standard in shoreline-mapping products, but quantifying the tide-attributable share of learned change-detector false events and fixing it by conditioning appears untested.
full_record.minimal_falsification_experiment: Assemble same-location image pairs over stable coasts spanning a range of predicted tide differences; run a public Siamese change detector; regress flagged-change area on tide delta; then fine-tune with tide-difference conditioning or tide-matched pairing and re-measure false events against injected true changes.
full_record.main_risk: Wave setup, wind-driven surge, and seasonal beach profiles deviate from harmonic predictions, capping the share of variance that predicted tide explains.
full_record.community_default_belief: [MODEL SPECULATION] The community treats coastal false changes as generic noise to be handled by more training data, not as a deterministic, exactly predictable astronomical covariate.
full_record.why_it_might_be_wrong: In micro-tidal seas the tide-attributable share may be too small to matter, restricting the fix to macro-tidal coasts.
full_record.fastest_falsification_experiment: Public data and model: Sentinel-2 coastal imagery with NOAA/FES-style public harmonic tide predictions and a public Siamese change-detection model (e.g., BIT pretrained on LEVIR-CD); evaluation plus light fine-tuning is under 10 GPU-hours on one consumer GPU (~$15).

family_fingerprint.manipulated_variable: tidal-stage matching and tide-height conditioning
family_fingerprint.measurement_family: false-change rate vs tide delta and recovery at fixed recall
