one_line_idea: UAV crop-monitoring orthomosaics carry a BRDF hotspot artifact: view-sun geometry varies across flight lines, imprinting periodic stripes into model predictions that follow solar geometry rather than the field — a quantifiable, correctable bias in precision-agriculture maps.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Models applied to UAV orthomosaics inherit flight-line-periodic prediction artifacts: predicted stress/weed/anomaly fractions oscillate at the flight-line spatial frequency in excess of any periodicity present in the labels, and the stripe phase aligns with the mosaic's view-sun geometry rather than with agronomic ground truth.

full_record.one_line_idea: UAV crop-monitoring orthomosaics carry a BRDF hotspot artifact: view-sun geometry varies across flight lines, imprinting periodic stripes into model predictions that follow solar geometry rather than the field — a quantifiable, correctable bias in precision-agriculture maps.
full_record.problem: [KNOWN FACT] Vegetation reflectance is strongly directional (BRDF), peaking near the hotspot where view and sun directions coincide; UAV orthomosaics stitch images taken at systematically varying view angles along parallel flight lines, so apparent canopy brightness varies within a single mosaic in a geometry-determined pattern.
full_record.core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Models applied to UAV orthomosaics inherit flight-line-periodic prediction artifacts: predicted stress/weed/anomaly fractions oscillate at the flight-line spatial frequency in excess of any periodicity present in the labels, and the stripe phase aligns with the mosaic's view-sun geometry rather than with agronomic ground truth.
full_record.falsifiable_prediction: [EXPECTED RESULT] Spectral analysis of predicted class-fraction maps along the across-track direction will show a peak at the flight-line frequency with amplitude >= 2x the same statistic computed on ground-truth labels for a majority of evaluated fields, and stripe phase will align with the view-geometry pattern above chance; kill the idea if predicted stripe amplitude is <= 1.2x label amplitude or if phase alignment is at chance.
full_record.why_important: Variable-rate application decisions are made directly from these maps, so geometry-induced stripes translate into misapplied fertilizer and herbicide; once measured, the artifact is deterministically correctable from flight and solar geometry.
full_record.why_possibly_novel: [MODEL SPECULATION / unverified] BRDF effects are established in satellite radiometry, but quantifying hotspot-induced striping in learned UAV prediction maps — and separating it from label periodicity — appears untested.
full_record.minimal_falsification_experiment: Run public segmentation baselines on public UAV/aerial agriculture datasets; compute across-track spatial spectra of predictions and labels; estimate flight-line direction from mosaic seams or metadata; test amplitude excess and phase alignment.
full_record.main_risk: Agronomic practices (drill rows, tramlines, sprayer tracks) are also periodic and must be separated from flight-line frequency by orientation and period, or the audit conflates management patterns with optics.
full_record.community_default_belief: [MODEL SPECULATION] Practitioners treat orthomosaics as radiometrically uniform maps and attribute within-field prediction patterns to real agronomic variation.
full_record.why_it_might_be_wrong: Mosaic blending and vignetting correction in modern photogrammetry pipelines may already suppress hotspot contrast below detectability.
full_record.fastest_falsification_experiment: Public data and model: WeedMap multispectral UAV orthomosaics and Agriculture-Vision aerial field imagery with a public U-Net/DeepLabv3+ baseline; inference plus spectral analysis is under 4 GPU-hours on one consumer GPU (~$6).

family_fingerprint.manipulated_variable: across-track spectral analysis of predictions vs labels with geometry alignment
family_fingerprint.measurement_family: flight-line stripe amplitude excess and phase alignment

one_line_idea: Cross-site failure in wheat-head detection is substantially a physical sampling mismatch: deterministic ground-sample-distance standardization closes a large share of the domain gap that heavy scale augmentation fails to close, and the residual correlates with non-scale factors.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] A substantial fraction of the cross-site AP drop is attributable to GSD mismatch rather than to agronomic or illumination differences, so deterministic standardization (resampling every site to a fixed centimeters-per-pixel, with per-site scale from metadata or median head size) recovers much of the gap, and per-site recovery scales with that site's GSD deviation from the training distribution.

full_record.one_line_idea: Cross-site failure in wheat-head detection is substantially a physical sampling mismatch: deterministic ground-sample-distance standardization closes a large share of the domain gap that heavy scale augmentation fails to close, and the residual correlates with non-scale factors.
full_record.problem: [KNOWN FACT] The Global Wheat Head Detection benchmark spans dozens of acquisition sites with different sensors and flight heights, hence different ground-sample distances; cross-site performance drop is the benchmark's central difficulty, and physical scale is a controllable variable given metadata or object-size statistics.
full_record.core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] A substantial fraction of the cross-site AP drop is attributable to GSD mismatch rather than to agronomic or illumination differences, so deterministic standardization (resampling every site to a fixed centimeters-per-pixel, with per-site scale from metadata or median head size) recovers much of the gap, and per-site recovery scales with that site's GSD deviation from the training distribution.
full_record.falsifiable_prediction: [EXPECTED RESULT] GSD standardization will close >= 35% of the mean cross-site AP drop for a fixed detector while random-scale augmentation at equal budget closes <= 20%, and per-site recovery will correlate with per-site GSD deviation at Spearman rho >= 0.5; kill the idea if standardization closes < 10% of the gap or fails to beat scale augmentation.
full_record.why_important: It would show that cheap deterministic physics beats expensive learned invariance on a flagship agricultural benchmark, and the recipe generalizes to any aerial task where metric scale is recoverable.
full_record.why_possibly_novel: [MODEL SPECULATION / unverified] Scale augmentation is the default remedy for size variation; an explicit attribution of the GWHD domain gap to GSD, with deterministic standardization as the intervention and a residual-factor analysis, appears untested.
full_record.minimal_falsification_experiment: Train a detector on GWHD source domains; evaluate held-out sites raw versus GSD-standardized; compare against a scale-jitter-augmented model at equal budget; correlate per-site recovery with GSD deviation.
full_record.main_risk: Per-site GSD metadata is incomplete, so scale must partly be estimated from head-size statistics, which assumes head sizes are comparable across genotypes and stages.
full_record.community_default_belief: [MODEL SPECULATION] The community default is that domain gaps in agricultural imagery are dominated by biology and illumination, requiring learned domain adaptation rather than deterministic resampling.
full_record.why_it_might_be_wrong: Wheat-head physical size genuinely varies across genotypes and growth stages, so size normalization could remove real signal along with the sampling artifact.
full_record.fastest_falsification_experiment: Public data and model: Global Wheat Head Detection 2021 with a YOLOv8 detector; two trainings plus cross-site evaluations are under 10 GPU-hours on one consumer GPU (~$15).

family_fingerprint.manipulated_variable: deterministic GSD standardization vs scale augmentation at equal budget
family_fingerprint.measurement_family: AP-gap closure fraction and GSD-deviation correlation
